STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.speaker: A minority
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.claim: A minority classifies most of the surah as Madinan but verses 68–70 as Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.anchor: while a minority consider most of the sūrah to be from the Madinan period and vv. 68–70 to be from the Makkan period

STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r8.claim: The Quraysh also ask why the Quran came gradually instead of all at once.
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r8.anchor: why the Quran was not sent down all at once, rather than being revealed gradually over years (v. 32)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p363/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p363/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p363/r3.claim: This section sets out the objections, their motives and consequences, adds further objections, and urges the Prophet and companions to ignore them patiently.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p363/r3.anchor: In this section, the afore-mentioned objections are cited, their motives are highlighted and the consequence of this blind animosity is also depicted.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r5.claim: Islahi identifies a fourth objection: opponents said a divine Qur’an should have been revealed all at once, reinforcing their claim that others coauthored it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r5.anchor: This verse cites their fourth objection. They would spread this propaganda against the Qur’ ān in the hearts of people

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r6.claim: God could reveal the whole Book at once, but the Prophet could not receive and bear it all at once, and people could not learn from it effectively.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r6.anchor: it would not have been possible for the Prophet (sws) to receive it at once nor could the people have been taught effectively.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r7.claim: The gradual lessons let the Prophet bear the Qur’an’s burden and gave willing learners an opportunity to learn.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r7.anchor: so that he could bear it and those who want to learn are provided with this opportunity.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r8.claim: Tartīl means reading and reciting in a very thorough manner.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r8.anchor: means to read and recite in a very thorough way.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r9.claim: The tartīl expression is coordinated with a verb suppressed after kadhalika.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r9.anchor: the verb which is suppressed after

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r10.claim: The careful, piecemeal lessons show divine favor, making gradual revelation a reason for gratitude rather than objection.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p373/r10.anchor: The implication is that the piecemeal revelation of the Qur’ ān should be a reason of expressing gratitude and not raising objections.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r1.claim: No divine scripture was revealed all at once: only the Ten Commandments came to Moses together on tablets, while the rest of the Torah was revealed during his life.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r1.anchor: Only the ten commandments were revealed in one instalment. They were given to Moses (sws) written on tablets.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r2.claim: The Gospel consists of Jesus’s wise sermons revealed on different occasions as needs arose, and the Psalms of David’s hymns and counsels were likewise revealed on separate occasions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r2.anchor: the Gospel is composed of the sagacious sermons of Jesus (sws) which were revealed to him at various instances according to the needs that arose.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r3.claim: Prophets were preachers, teachers, and moral mentors charged with reforming an ailing nation, so they received guidance gradually as needed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r3.anchor: They were preachers, teachers and moral mentors. They had to cure an ailing nation and purify their beliefs and deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r4.claim: No People of the Book scholar, as far as Islahi knows, claims that their scriptures were revealed at once; such a claim would contradict those books.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r4.anchor: none of the scholars of the People of the Book has ever claimed if any of their books was revealed at once.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r5.claim: Islahi rejects the exegetes’ opinion that the Torah, Psalms, and Gospel were each revealed all at once.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p374/r5.anchor: The opinion of our exegetes who say that the Torah, Psalms and the Gospel were revealed in one go is thus not correct too.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r7.claim: The disbelievers’ demand that the Qur’an come all at once is a proposal and objection revealing their aversion to truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r7.anchor: وقالوا أي الكفار على سبيل الاقتراح والاعتراض الدال على نفورهم عن الحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says نزل here must mean أنزل; if it retained its ordinary sense of gradual revelation, the wording would contradict itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r8.anchor: قال الزمخشري: نزل هاهنا بمعنى أنزل لا غير كخبر بمعنى أخبر وإلا كان متدافعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the restriction: for him, doubled نزل is synonymous with أنزل, so no contradiction arises.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r9.anchor: وقد بينا ذلك في أول آل عمران وقائل ذلك كفار قريش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r10.claim: The apparent speakers are Quraysh, who argued that a revelation from God would have come as one whole, like the Torah and Gospel; identifying them as Jews is said to be pointless.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r10.anchor: وقيل: قائلو ذلك اليهود وهذا قول لا طائل تحته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r11.claim: The challenge’s miraculous force does not depend on whether revelation came all at once; piecemeal revelation makes the challenge clearer because they were asked to match one sura and failed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r11.anchor: بل الإعجاز في نزوله مفرقا أظهر إذ يطالبون بمعارضة سورة منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r12.claim: One reading makes “like that” the disbelievers’ reference to revelation of the Torah and Gospel as a single whole; “to strengthen your heart” then explains an omitted statement that the Qur’an was divided across times.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r12.anchor: فقيل: هو من كلام الكفار وأشاروا إلى التوراة والإنجيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r13.claim: Alternatively, “like that” begins God’s own reply to the implied question of why revelation came gradually: He sent it gradually to strengthen the Prophet’s heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103/r13.anchor: وقيل: هو مستأنف من كلام الله تعالى لا من كلامهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says gradual revelation strengthens the Prophet’s heart and enables step-by-step memorization; unlike literate David, Moses, and Jesus, the unlettered Prophet needed to receive and retain it orally. It came over twenty or twenty-three years, with events and questions, and gradual revelation permits abrogating and abrogated verses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r1.anchor: والحكمة فيه أن نقوي بتفريقه فؤادك حتى تعيه وتحفظه لأن المتلقن إنما يقوى قلبه على حفظ العلم شيئا بعد شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r2.claim: The lām in لنثبت is causal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r2.anchor: واللام في لنثبت به لام العلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r3.claim: Abu Hatim calls it an oath lām, reading the sense as “By God, He will surely strengthen,” with the nūn deleted and the lām kasra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: هي لام القسم والتقدير والله ليثبتن فحذفت النون وكسرت اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls Abu Hatim’s parsing extremely weak and says it depends on al-Akhfash’s disfavored claim that an oath’s answer can take lām kay, as in 68:43.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r4.anchor: وهذا قول في غاية الضعف وكان ينحو إلى مذهب الأخفش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r5.claim: ʿAbd Allah reads ليثبت, with God as the subject: “so that God may strengthen.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ليثبت بالياء أي ليثبت الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r6.claim: رتلناه means “We separated it”; another explanation is “We made it clear,” and another “We explained it.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p103#2/r6.anchor: ورتلناه أي فصلناه. وقيل: بيناه. وقيل: فسرناه

SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r1.claim: Jumlata is a circumstantial accusative describing the Qurʾān, with the sense of its being brought down all together.
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r1.anchor: حال من القرآن، إذ هي في معنى مجتمعا

SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r2.claim: One parse puts kathālika in a nominative position: the matter is so; li-nuthabbita then gives the reason for an omitted verb, we did that to strengthen your heart.
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r2.anchor: إما مرفوعة المحل أي: الأمر كذلك

SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r3.claim: Alternatively kathālika is a circumstantial accusative meaning it was sent down in that manner, or it qualifies an omitted verbal noun; li-nuthabbita attaches to that omitted verb.
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r3.anchor: وإما منصوبته على الحال أي: أنزل مثل ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r4.claim: Abū Ḥātim calls kathālika the answer to an oath; al-Samīn judges this weak and says al-Akhfash took that approach for wa-li-taṣghā as well.
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: " هي جواب قسم " وهذا قول مرجوح

SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r5.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r5.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads liyuthbita with yāʾ, making God the subject.
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله " ليثبت " بالياء أي: الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r6.claim: Tartīl means separating or spacing things out, including the succession of one word after another with a slight pause but no break in breath.
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r6.anchor: والترتيل: التفريق. ومجيء الكلمة بعد الأخرى بسكون يسير

SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r7.claim: The word ratal for teeth describes slight spaces between them, as in thaghr ratil or murattal.
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r7.anchor: ومنه ثغر رتل ومرتل أي: مفلج الأسنان

SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes nuzzila here to mean anzala, without an implication of gradual revelation, to avoid conflict with the demand that the Qurʾān come all at once.
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r8.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ونزل هنا بمعنى: أنزل لا غير

SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r9.claim: Al-Samīn says al-Zamakhsharī's argument assumes the intensive pattern signals distribution or gradualness; earlier discussions and an Ibn ʿAbbās report seem to support this on the surface.
SAMIN-DURR:25:32/r9.anchor: وهذا بناء منه على معتقده وهو أن التضعيف يدل على التفريق

ZAJJAJ:v4p66/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p66/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p66/r1.claim: The critics ask why the Qur'an was not revealed all at once, as the Torah was; revelation took twenty years, and its gradual delivery strengthened the Prophet's heart.
ZAJJAJ:v4p66/r1.anchor: وكان بين أول نزول القرآن وآخره عشرون سنة، فقالوا: لم لم ينزل جملة واحدة كما أنزلت التوراة:

ZAJJAJ:v4p66/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p66/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p66/r2.claim: كذلك means that God revealed it gradually for the purpose of strengthening the Prophet's heart.
ZAJJAJ:v4p66/r2.anchor: أي أنزلناه كذلك متفرقا، لأن معنى قولهم: (لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة) يدل على معنى لم نزل عليه القرآن متفرقا

ZAJJAJ:v4p66/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p66/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p66/r3.claim: Tartīl means measured, deliberate delivery, the opposite of haste.
ZAJJAJ:v4p66/r3.anchor: (ورتلناه ترتيلا). أي نزلناه على الترتيل، وهو ضد العجلة، وهو التمكث.

ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n26/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n26/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n26/r1.claim: Muhammad's opponents implied that gradual revelation showed he had composed the Qur'an to suit changing personal and political needs.
ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n26/r1.anchor: the gradual, step-by-step revelation of the Qur'an points to its having been "composed" by Muhammad to suit his changing personal and political requirements.

ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n27/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n27/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n27/r1.claim: Rattalnahu tartilan conveys assembling and well arranging the parts of something and giving it inner consistency; Asad compares 4:82 and 39:23.
ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n27/r1.anchor: The concise phrase rattalnahu tartilan comprises the parallel concepts of "putting the component parts [of a thing] together and arranging them well" as well as "endowing it with inner consistency".

ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n27/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n27/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n27/r2.claim: Consistency across the Prophet's eventful twenty-three years indicates divine inspiration, strengthens thoughtful believers, and is the deepest reason for gradual revelation.
ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n27/r2.anchor: it is bound to strengthen the faith of every thinking believer: and herein lies, according to the Qur'an itself, the deepest reason

ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n27/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n27/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n27/r3.claim: When used of Qur'an recitation, tartil means measured diction and thoughtful enunciation, as in 73:4.
ASAD-NOTES:25:32#n27/r3.anchor: the term tartil refers to the measured diction and the thoughtful manner in which it ought to be enunciated.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r2.speaker: مسلم بن جندب
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r2.claim: Muslim b. Jundab taught thirty verses in the morning and thirty in the evening.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r2.anchor: وقال كان مسلم بن جندب يقرأ علينا غدوة ثلاثين آية وعشية ثلاثين آية

IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r3.speaker: قالون
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r3.claim: Qālūn says Medinans did not use hamza until Ibn Jundab introduced it in mustahziʾūn and istuhziʾa.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r3.anchor: قالون قال كان أهل المدينة لا يهمزون حتى همز ابن جندب فهمزوا مستهزئون واستهزىء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r4.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r4.claim: The source labels a report from al-Zubayr as mursal: they prayed Friday with the Prophet, then hurried to the open ground, where scarcely a foot-space remained.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r4.anchor: عن الزبير قال كنا نصلي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الجمعة فنبتدر الأجم وما هو إلا موضع قدم هذا مرسل

IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r5.claim: Yazīd b. Rūmān was a Medinan jurist, a client of the family of al-Zubayr, and chiefly known for Qurʾān recitation.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r5.anchor: ومنهم يزيد بن رومان وكان يزيد من فقهاء أهل المدينة وهو مولى لآل الزبير بن العوام وكان الغالب عليه القرآن

IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r6.speaker: يزيد بن رومان
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r6.claim: Yazīd b. Rūmān received the reading directly from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAyyāsh b. Abī Rabīʿa and also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r6.anchor: أخبرني يزيد بن رومان مولى آل الزبير أنه أخذ القراءة عرضا عن عبد الله بن عياش بن أبي ربيعة وقد روى أيضا عن ابن عباس

IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r7.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r7.claim: Nāfiʿ names ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Hurmuz, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba b. Niṣāḥ, Muslim b. Jundab, and Yazīd b. Rūmān as Medinan reading imams he encountered.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r7.anchor: فهؤلاء الذين ذكر نافع أنه أدركهم بالمدينة من الأئمة في القراءة عبد الرحمن بن هرمر وأبو جعفر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r8.speaker: يوسف بن عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r8.claim: Yūsuf b. ʿAmr reports that Nāfiʿ also read to Ṣāliḥ b. Khawwāt.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r8.anchor: أخبرني يوسف بن عمرو أن نافعا قرأ على صالح بن خوات أخبره بذلك عبد الملك بن مسلمة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r9.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r9.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r9.claim: Nāfiʿ said that he read to seventy Successors.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p59/r9.anchor: سمعت نافعا يقول قرأت على سبعين من التابعين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r1.claim: Ḥamza was the leading reader of Kufa in his era; Sufyān al-Thawrī and many major Kufans studied the reading with him.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r1.anchor: وكان حمزة إمام أهل الكوفة في عصره أخذ القراءة عنه سفيان الثوري وقرأ عليه جلة أهل الكوفة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r2.speaker: شعيب بن حرب
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r2.claim: Shuʿayb b. Ḥarb says Ḥamza led the prayer in 100 AH and Sufyān al-Thawrī recited the Qurʾān to him four times.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r2.anchor: قال محمد بن الهيثم المقرىء أخبرني الحسن بن بكار أنه سمع شعيب بن حرب يقول أم حمزة الناس سنة مائة وإن سفيان الثوري درس على حمزة القرآن أربع درسات

IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r3.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r3.claim: Ḥamza says Sufyān presented the Qurʾān to him four times, and ʿAlī b. Ṣāliḥ came asking him to teach recitation.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r3.anchor: حدثني حمزة الزيات أن سفيان الثوري عرض عليه القرآن أربع عرضات

IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r4.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r4.claim: Ḥamza said that ʿAlī b. Ṣāliḥ came and asked him to teach him recitation.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r4.anchor: وقال حمزة أتاني علي بن صالح فسألني أن أقرئه

IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r5.speaker: أبو هشام
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r5.claim: Abū Hishām names the strongest early pupils of Ḥamza as Ibrāhīm al-Azraq, Khālid al-Ṭabīb, Khallād al-Aḥwal, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Ḥammād; many preferred Ibrāhīm to Sulaym, while ʿAbd al-Raḥmān was the most knowledgeable about the Qurʾān’s technical grounds.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r5.anchor: عن أبي هشام قال كان أقرأ من قرأ على حمزة في الزمن الأول أربعة إبراهيم الأزرق

IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r6.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r6.claim: Sulaym al-Abrash was another pupil of Ḥamza, though not equal to the four leading pupils.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r6.anchor: وكان آخر ولم يكن مثلهم يقال له سلم الأبرش

IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r7.speaker: أبو هشام الرفاعي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r7.claim: Al-Kisāʾī mastered the reading from Ḥamza, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Ḥammād read to al-Kisāʾī.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r7.anchor: قال أبو هشام الرفاعي ضبط الكسائي القراءة على حمزة وعبد الرحمن ابن أبي حماد قرأ عليه يعني على الكسائي

IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r8.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r8.claim: Ḥamza said he never read a single letter without transmitted precedent.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r8.anchor: سمعت حمزة يقول ما قرأت حرفا قط إلا بأثر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r9.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r9.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r9.claim: The author characterizes Ḥamza as following the imams’ transmitted practice and as knowledgeable about readings and their schools.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r9.anchor: وكان حمزة متبعا لآثار من أدرك من أئمة القراء عالما بالقراءة ومذاهبها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r10.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r10.speaker: سفيان
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r10.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī endorsed Ḥamza’s transmission-based practice, saying he read no Qurʾānic letter without an athar.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r10.anchor: قال سفيان أترون هذا ما قرأ حرفا من كتاب الله إلا بأثر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r11.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r11.speaker: محمد بن الهيثم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r11.claim: Muḥammad b. al-Haytham says Ḥamza’s reading dominated Kufa’s mosques; he did not recall a circle there reading ʿĀṣim’s reading.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p74/r11.anchor: سمعت محمد بن الهيثم المقرىء يقول أدركت الكوفة ومسجدها الغالب عليه قراءة حمزة ولا أعلمني أدركت حلقة من حلق المسجد الجامع يقرءون قراءة عاصم

NASHR:v1p32/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p32/r1.speaker: بعضهم
NASHR:v1p32/r1.claim: Some say the seven dialects were allowed early to ease recitation, then readers converged on the final presentation when one reading became easy for them.
NASHR:v1p32/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إن الترخيص في الأحرف السبعة كان في أول الإسلام لما في المحافظة على حرف واحد من المشقة عليهم أولا

NASHR:v1p32/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p32/r2.speaker: بعضهم
NASHR:v1p32/r2.claim: Another view holds that readings outside the final presentation were abrogated.
NASHR:v1p32/r2.anchor: وبعضهم يقول إنه نسخ ما سوى ذلك

NASHR:v1p32/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p32/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p32/r3.claim: Many scholars regarded readings attributed to Ubayy, Ibn Masud, and others that conflict with the codices as abrogated.
NASHR:v1p32/r3.anchor: ولذلك نص كثير من العلماء على أن الحروف التي وردت عن أبي وابن مسعود وغيرهما مما يخالف هذه المصاحف منسوخة

NASHR:v1p32/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p32/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p32/r4.claim: The claim that Ibn Masud allowed reading by paraphrase is false; he said the readings are close and people should recite as they had been taught.
NASHR:v1p32/r4.anchor: نظرت القراءات فوجدتهم متقاربين فاقرءوا كما علمتم

NASHR:v1p32/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p32/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p32/r5.claim: Companions sometimes inserted or wrote explanatory tafsir alongside recitation because they knew what they had received from the Prophet and feared no confusion.
NASHR:v1p32/r5.anchor: كانوا ربما يدخلون التفسير في القراءة إيضاحا وبيانا لأنهم محققون لما تلقوه عن النبي

NASHR:v1p32/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p32/r6.speaker: مسروق
NASHR:v1p32/r6.claim: Masruq reports that Ibn Masud disliked tafsir being inserted into the Quran; another transmitter quotes him urging that the Quran be kept free of additions.
NASHR:v1p32/r6.anchor: فروى مسروق عنه أنه كان يكره التفسير في القرآن

NASHR:v1p32/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p32/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
NASHR:v1p32/r7.claim: In a sound report through Zur ibn Hubaysh, Ibn Abbas says the Prophet presented the Quran to Gabriel annually and twice in his final year; Ibn Masud witnessed what was abrogated and changed, so his reading was the final one.
NASHR:v1p32/r7.anchor: قال لي ابن عباس أي القراءتين تقرأ؟

NASHR:v1p32/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p32/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p32/r8.claim: The Companions wrote what they verified as Quran and as un-abrogated, including soundly transmitted material not known to belong to the final presentation; this accounts for some codex differences.
NASHR:v1p32/r8.anchor: وإذ قد ثبت ذلك فلا إشكال أن الصحابة كتبوا في هذه المصاحف ما تحققوا أنه قرآن

NASHR:v1p32/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p32/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p32/r9.claim: If the Companions had written only the final presentation, the codices would not differ through additions and omissions; they left aside what they had not verified.
NASHR:v1p32/r9.anchor: إذ لو كانت العرضة الأخيرة فقط لم تختلف المصاحف بزيادة ونقص وغير ذلك

NASHR:v1p58#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p58#3/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p58#3/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jazari describes this second Andalusian transmission chain for al-Dani's al-Taysir as sound and elevated, reaching the author through Andalusians.

NASHR:v1p113/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p113/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p113/r1.claim: Warsh was deaf but could hear Quran recitation; he read Nafi's reading repeatedly and wrote it down. Nafi once directed him to wait by a pillar for a reader.

NASHR:v1p113/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p113/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p113/r2.claim: Warsh was born in 110 AH and died in Egypt in 197; after four complete readings with Nafi in Medina in 155, he returned to Egypt and became its leading recitation authority.
NASHR:v1p113/r2.anchor: وتوفي ورش بمصر سنة سبع وتسعين ومائة

NASHR:v1p113/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p113/r3.speaker: يونس بن عبد الأعلى
NASHR:v1p113/r3.claim: Yunus ibn Abd al-Ala praises Warsh's recitation, noting its clear hamza, lengthening, doubling, and grammatical articulation without tiring listeners.
NASHR:v1p113/r3.anchor: يونس بن عبد الأعلى كان ورش جيد القراءة حسن الصوت

NASHR:v1p113/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p113/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p113/r4.claim: Abu Nishit died in 258 AH and was a trustworthy, precise, distinguished reciter; Ibn Abi Hatim called him truthful.
NASHR:v1p113/r4.anchor: وتوفي أبو نشيط سنة ثمان وخمسين ومائتين ووهم من قال غير ذلك

NASHR:v1p113/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p113/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p113/r5.claim: Al-Halwani died in 250 AH and was a major, reliable expert, especially in the Qalun and Hisham transmissions; he traveled to Qalun in Medina twice.
NASHR:v1p113/r5.anchor: وتوفي الحلواني سنة خمسين ومائتين وكان أستاذا كبيرا إماما في القراءات

NASHR:v1p113/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p113/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p113/r6.claim: Ibn Buwayan was born in 260 AH, died in 344, and was reliable and precise; Ibn Ghalbun's spelling of his name as Thuban is a corruption.
NASHR:v1p113/r6.anchor: وتوفي ابن بويان سنة أربع وأربعين وثلاثمائة ومولده سنة ستين ومائتين

NASHR:v1p113/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p113/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p113/r7.claim: Al-Qazzaz, whose death before 340 AH is given tentatively, was a trustworthy and highly exacting reciter.
NASHR:v1p113/r7.anchor: وتوفي القزاز فيما أحسب قبل الأربعين وثلاثمائة

NASHR:v1p113/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p113/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p113/r8.claim: Ibn al-Ashath died shortly before 300 AH according to al-Dhahabi and was a reliable authority uniquely proficient in Qalun's reading from Abu Nishit.
NASHR:v1p113/r8.anchor: وتوفي ابن الأشعث قبيل الثلاثمائة فيما قال الذهبي

NASHR:v1p113/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p113/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p113/r9.claim: Ibn Abi Mihran died in 289 AH and was a skilled, trustworthy reciter.
NASHR:v1p113/r9.anchor: وتوفي ابن أبي مهران سنة تسع وثمانين ومائتين وكان مقرئا ماهرا ثقة حاذقا

NASHR:v1p113/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p113/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p113/r10.claim: Jaafar ibn Muhammad died around 290 AH and was dependable in the Qalun transmission.
NASHR:v1p113/r10.anchor: وتوفي جعفر بن محمد في حدود التسعين ومائتين وكان قيما برواية قالون ضابطا لها

NASHR:v1p113/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p113/r11.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p113/r11.claim: Al-Azraq died around 240 AH, was reliable and precise, and succeeded Warsh in Egypt. He read with Warsh for a long time, completing twenty recitations in both rapid and measured styles; al-Khuzai says Egypt and the Maghrib knew no Warsh route but his.
NASHR:v1p113/r11.anchor: وتوفي الأزرق في حدود سنة أربعين ومائتين وكان محققا ثقة ذا ضبط وإتقان

NASHR:v1p149/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p149/r1.speaker: بعضهم
NASHR:v1p149/r1.claim: Some performance scholars said Shuayb and Abu Hamdun only heard individual reading variants from Yahya ibn Adam, rather than presenting the Quran to him.
NASHR:v1p149/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إنما قرآ عليه الحروف فقط

NASHR:v1p149/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p149/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p149/r2.claim: Ibn al-Jazari says Shuayb heard the variants, whereas Abu Hamdun presented the Quran to Yahya ibn Adam; this is his preferred account over the claim that both only heard variants.
NASHR:v1p149/r2.anchor: والصحيح أن شعيبا سمع منه الحروف

NASHR:v1p151/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p151/r1.speaker: كثير من أهل الأداء
NASHR:v1p151/r1.claim: Many performance scholars say al-Ulaymi and Yahya ibn Adam both presented the Quran to Abu Bakr Shuba; another view says they only heard variants.
NASHR:v1p151/r1.anchor: وعرضا فيما أطلقه كثير من أهل الأداء على أبي بكر شعبة بن عياش

NASHR:v1p151/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p151/r2.speaker: بعضهم
NASHR:v1p151/r2.claim: Some authorities deny that al-Ulaymi and Yahya ibn Adam presented the Quran to Shuba and say they only heard variants from him.
NASHR:v1p151/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إنهما لم يعرضا عليه القرآن

NASHR:v1p151/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p151/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p151/r3.claim: Ibn al-Jazari distinguishes the transmissions: Yahya ibn Adam heard the variants from Shuba, while al-Ulaymi presented the Quran to him.
NASHR:v1p151/r3.anchor: والصحيح أن يحيى بن آدم روى عنه الحروف سماعا

NASHR:v1p151/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p151/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p151/r4.claim: Al-Dani says Ibn Mujahid recognized only al-Asha as having recited the full Quran to Abu Bakr, but asserts five others also did, naming four in this excerpt.

QIRAAT-ER:25:32:8#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:25:32:8#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:25:32:8#1/r1.claim: The hamza-less qurān form is a phonological simplification without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:25:32:8#1/r1.anchor: hmz, mutawatir: Hamza dropped — reading without hamza (tashīl/ibdāl); no semantic change

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p69/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p69/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p69/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the Qur’an came down in one or several verses at a time, often answering questions or replying to what people said to the Prophet; its revelation spanned about twenty years.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p69/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن الحسن في قوله ﴿ ورتلناه ترتيلا ﴾ قال كان ينزل آيه أو آيتين أو آيات كان ينزل جوابا لهم إذا سألوا عن شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the disbelievers as the polytheists already mentioned; they are called disbelievers to condemn them and signal the cause of their objection. Another view identifies a group of Jews.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r1.anchor: والمراد بهم المشركون كما صح عن ابن عباس وهم القائلون أولا والتعبير عنهم بعنوان الكفر لذمهم به

ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r2.claim: Their challenge means, “Why was the Qur’an not revealed to him all at once?” The wording can mean revelation as a report, with no gradual delivery intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r2.anchor: أي أنزل عليه كخبر بمعنى أخبر فلا قصد فيه إلى التدريج

ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r3.claim: “All at once” is a circumstantial accusative, and wāḥidah is an emphatic adjective; reading the challenge as asking for a single collective division would contradict the demand for one whole.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r3.anchor: فإنه لو قصد ذلك لتدافعا إذ يكون المعنى لولا فرق القرآن جملة واحدة والتفريق ينافي الجملية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r4.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r4.claim: Hadiths and early reports indicate that the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms were revealed all at once; al-Suyuti says this was nearly consensus, rejecting Ibn al-Kamal’s claim that the Torah came gradually over eighteen years.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r4.anchor: كما أنزلت التوراة والانجيل والزبور على ما تدل عليه الأحاديث والآثار حتى كاد يكون اجماعا كما قال السيوطي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r5.speaker: ابن الكمال
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Kamal argues that the Torah was revealed in stages over eighteen years, citing its own texts; al-Alusi says no decisive Qur’anic or Prophetic proof supports the contrary and attributes the claim to incomplete research.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r5.anchor: فتقول ابن الكمال إن التوراة أنزلت منجمة في ثماني عشرة سنة ويدل عليه نصوص التوراة ولا قاطع بخلافه من الكتاب والسنة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r6.claim: The objection has little force: the Qur’an’s inimitability is unaffected by whole or gradual revelation, and gradual delivery has benefits that the verse itself proceeds to explain.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r6.anchor: وهذا الاعتراض مما لا طائل تحته لأن الاعجاز مما لا يختلف بنزوله جملة أو مفرقا مع أن للتفريق فوائد منها ما ذكره الله تعالى بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r7.claim: One argument says the Qur’an’s truth is proven by its inimitable eloquence, which matches each passage to its circumstances, a match said to be impossible if it came all at once; al-Alusi contests that premise in the next segment.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p14#2/r7.anchor: وقيل : إن شاهد صحة القرآن اعجازه وذلك ببلاغته وهي بمطابقته لمقتضى الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r1.claim: Al-Alusi denies that eloquence matching circumstances requires gradual revelation: a single revelation could match each passage to later events; the Qur’an did descend all at once to the lowest heaven, which would otherwise imply a non-inimitable portion, and this may heighten its miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r1.anchor: وفيه أن قوله : ولا يتيسر الخ منوع فانه يجوز أن ينزل دفعة واحدة مع رعاية المطابقة المذكورة في كل جملة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r2.claim: The clause is God’s reply to the objection, explaining one wisdom in gradual revelation; kādhālika is an adverbial description of the implied revelation, or may be circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r2.anchor: كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك استئناف وارد من جهته تعالى لرد مقالتهم وبيان بعض الحكم في تنزيله تدريجيا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r3.claim: Gradual revelation strengthened the Prophet’s heart by easing memorization, understanding, and precise retention, showing successive wisdoms, repeatedly bringing Gabriel, and renewing the challenge to critics with each passage.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r3.anchor: فان في تنزيله مفرقا تيسيرا لحفظ النظم وفهم المعاني وضبط الكلام والوقوف على تفاصيل ما روعي فيه من الحكم والمصالح

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r4.claim: Further benefits of gradual revelation include distinguishing later abrogating verses from earlier abrogated ones and combining situational clues with verbal evidence to recognize eloquence suited to context.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r4.anchor: منها معرفة الناسخ المتأخر نزوله من المنسوخ المتقدم نزوله المخالف لحكمه ومنها انضمام القرائن الحالية إلى الدلالات اللفظية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r5.claim: An alternative makes kādhālika part of the disbelievers’ statement, with the comparison describing the Qur’an or the manner of its revelation and referring to the earlier scriptures.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r5.anchor: وقيل : قووله تعالى ( كذلك ) من تمام كلام الكفرة والكاف نصب على الحال من القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r6.speaker: أبو حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r6.claim: Abu Hatim calls the lām an oath particle, reconstructing “By God, We shall surely establish”; al-Alusi, citing Abu Hayyan, calls this extremely weak and rejects the related Akhfash analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r6.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم : هي لام القسم والتقدير والله لنثبتن

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r7.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r7.claim: Abd Allah reads liyuthabbit, with yāʾ, meaning “so that God may make firm.”
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15/r7.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ليثبت بالياء أي ليثبت الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r1.claim: The clause coordinates with an omitted verb whose cause was stated; the indefinite form of ترتيلا magnifies the remarkable manner of recitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r1.anchor: عطف على الفعل المحذوف المعلل بما ذكر وتنكير ترتيلا للتفخيم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r2.claim: God revealed the Quran in that manner and arranged it in an incomparable, beautiful tartil, separating it verse by verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r2.anchor: كذلك نزلناه ورتلناه ترتيلا بديعا لايقادر قدره وترتيله تفريقه ءاية بعد ءاية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r3.speaker: النخعي والحسن وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r3.claim: They explain tartil as dividing the revelation verse after verse.

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Quran was made clear with measured, unhurried explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : بيناه بيانا فيه ترسل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r5.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi glosses tartil as setting the Quran out in detail.

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r6.claim: Mujahid explains it as making one part follow another.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد : جعلنا بعضه إثر بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r7.claim: An alternative takes the phrase as an instruction to recite the Quran in measured tartil, as in 73:4.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r7.anchor: هو الأمر بترتيل قراءته بقوله تعالى : ( ورتل القرآن ترتيلا )

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r8.claim: Another explanation is that Gabriel recited it to Muhammad gradually over twenty or twenty-three years, deliberately and patiently.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r8.anchor: قرأناه عليك بلسان جبريل عليه السلام شيئا فشيئا في عشرين أو ثلاثة وعشرين سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r9.claim: The term is likened to spaced teeth: مرتل describes teeth whose gaps keep them from being contiguous.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p15#2/r9.anchor: مأخوذ من قولهم : ثغر مرتل أي مفلج الأسنان غير متلاصقها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r3.speaker: الذين كفروا
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r3.claim: The disbelievers objected that the Quran should have been sent all at once, as the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms were sent to Moses, Jesus, and David.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r3.anchor: وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة} كما أنزلت التوراة على موسى والإنجيل على عيسى والزبور على داود

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r4.claim: God says that He sent the Quran in portions in this way to strengthen the Prophet's heart.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r4.anchor: قال الله تعالى: {كذلك} فعلت، {لنثبت به فؤادك}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r5.claim: Gradual revelation strengthened the Prophet's heart so that he could absorb and memorize it; unlike earlier recipients, he was an unlettered prophet who could neither write nor read.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r5.anchor: أي: أنزلناه متفرقا ليقوى به قلبك فتعيه وتحفظه، فإن الكتب أنزلت على الأنبياء يكتبون ويقرءون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r6.claim: Because the Quran includes abrogating and abrogated material and answers to questions, it was divided to aid the Prophet's retention and make acting upon it easier.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r6.anchor: ولأن من القرآن الناسخ والمنسوخ، ومنه ما هو جواب لمن سأل عن أمور، ففرقناه ليكون أوعى لرسول الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses tartil as making the revelation clear.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r8.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says the Quran was divided in detail.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r9.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r9.claim: Mujahid explains that the revelation came some of it after some of it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بعضه في إثر بعض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r10.speaker: النخعي والحسن وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r10.claim: Al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan, and Qatada say it was divided piece by piece, verse after verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p83/r10.anchor: وقال النخعي والحسن وقتادة: فرقناه تفريقا، آية بعد آية

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r4.claim: The verb is understood as passive anzala, as in a verb meaning reported, so it does not conflict with the demand for one descent.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r4.anchor: أي أنزل عليه كخبر بمعنى أخبر لئلا يناقض قوله: { جملة وحدة }

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r5.claim: The objection has no force: the Qur'an's miraculousness is unchanged whether revealed all at once or in parts.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r5.anchor: لأن الإعجاز لا يختلف بنزوله جملة أو مفرقا

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r6.claim: Gradual revelation strengthened Muhammad's heart for memorization and understanding; unlike Moses, David, and Jesus, he was unlettered and might have been overwhelmed by an all-at-once revelation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r6.anchor: فتقوى بتفريقه فؤادك على حفظه وفهمه

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r7.claim: Revelation with events gave deeper insight; each installment that opponents could not match strengthened his heart.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r7.anchor: ولأن نزوله بحسب الوقائع يوجب مزيد بصيرة وغوص في المعنى

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r8.claim: Gabriel's repeated arrival strengthened the Prophet; gradual revelation also disclosed abrogation and joined situational context to verbal evidence, aiding eloquence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r8.anchor: ولأنه إذا نزل به جبريل حالا بعد حال يثبت به فؤاده

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r9.claim: Kadhālika may refer to omitted gradual sending, or remain part of the disbelievers' speech and refer to earlier books; the lām attaches to an omitted phrase either way.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r9.anchor: وكذلك صفة مصدر محذوف والإشارة إلى إنزاله مفرقا

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r10.claim: God recited the Qur'an to Muhammad bit by bit, deliberately and calmly, over twenty or twenty-three years.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r10.anchor: وقرأناه عليك شيئا بعد شيء على تؤدة وتمهل

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r11.claim: The root image of tartīl is the spacing of the teeth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:31-32/r11.anchor: وأصل الترتيل في الأسنان وهو تفليجها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p314/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p314/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p314/r6.claim: The disbelievers' objection follows the complaint that they abandoned the Qurʾān and the assurance of God's aid; the explicit label 'those who disbelieved' highlights the trait behind their speech.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p314/r6.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه شكايته من هجرانهم للقرآن , وقرر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p314/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p314/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p314/r7.claim: The disbelievers hide envy and hostility behind their demand for one-time revelation, although their reason recognizes the Qurʾān as God's inimitable speech whether revealed in parts or all at once.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p314/r7.anchor: القرآن كلام لإعجازه لهم متفرقا , فضلا عن كونه مجتمعا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p314/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p314/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p314/r8.claim: They also conceal the clear effects of the Qurʾān that testify to God's oneness and other divine attributes.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p314/r8.anchor: وغطوا ما وضح لهم من آثاره الظاهرة الشاهد بوحدانيته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r1.claim: Lowlā means ‘why not?’ or ‘if only,’ expressing the disbelievers’ objection.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r1.anchor: { لو لا } أي هلا . ولما كانوا لشدة ضعفهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r2.claim: They use the passive ‘was sent down’ because they scarcely concede that the Qur’an is revelation, much less that God sent it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r2.anchor: بنوا للمفعول في هذه الشبهة التي أوردها قولهم : { نزل عليه } ولما عبروا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r3.claim: The intensive form suggests gradual descent; they invoke it to attract listeners, then clarify that they want the opposite.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r3.anchor: ولما عبروا بصيغة التفعيل المشيرة إلى التدريج والتفريق استجلابا للسامع لئلا يعرض عنهم ,

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r4.claim: They stress a single, complete descent from beginning to end to prove divine origin and dispel their suspicion that Muhammad arranged it gradually.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r4.anchor: ثم صرحوا بالمراد بقولهم : { جملة } وأكدوا بقولهم : { واحدة } أي من أوله إلى آخره بمرة , ليتحقق أنه من عند الله ,

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r5.claim: Gradual revelation steadies the Prophet through repeated communication from God and enables him and his followers to understand the meanings.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r5.anchor: بالإغاثة بتردد الرسل بيننا وبينك , وبتكمينك وتمكين أتباعك من تفهم المعاني ,

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r6.claim: Gradual descent eases the rulings for Muslims and accommodates the wisdom and benefits of abrogation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r6.anchor: تخفيفا للأحكام , في تحميلها أهل الإسلام , بالتدريج على حسب المصالح , واتنافي الحكمة في الناسخ والمنسوخ ,

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r7.claim: A piecemeal revelation also facilitates memorization for an ummi community that neither reads nor writes and supplies answers when needed.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r7.anchor: وتسهيا للحفظ لا سيما والأمة أمية لا تقرأ ولا تكتب , وتلقينا للأجوبه في أوقاتها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r8.claim: Revealing portions separately strengthens the Qur’an’s inimitability: inability to answer a challenge involving one portion proves inability to answer a greater one.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r8.anchor: وتعظيما للإعجاز , لأن ما تحدى بنجم منه فعجز عنه علم أن العجز عن أكثر منه أولى ,

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r9.claim: The Qur’an was sent down gradually in this excellent manner; its advantages make the objection pointless and reveal the objectors’ narrowness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r9.anchor: فالحاصل أن التفريق أدخل في باب الإعجاز وفي كل حكمة , فعلم أن هذا الاعتراض فضول ومماراة بما لا طائل تحته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r10.claim: The demonstrative does not refer to earlier scriptures: the Torah too was revealed in stages, as Biqāʿī says he established from its text in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r10.anchor: وليست الإشارة محتملة لأن تكون للكتب الماضية , لأن نزولها إنما كان منجما كما بينته في سورة النساء عن نص التوراة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r11.claim: Biqāʿī says the Qur’an’s staged revelation extended over more than twenty years.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r11.anchor: أي فرقناه في الإنزال إليك تفريقا في نيف وعشرين سنة ؛ وقال البغوي : قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : بيناه بيانا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r12.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r12.claim: Al-Baghawī transmits Ibn ʿAbbās’s explanation that tartīl means making the message clear, with deliberation and steadiness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r12.anchor: وقال البغوي : قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : بيناه بيانا , والنرتيل : التبين في ترسل وتثبت انتهى .

BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r13.claim: Tartīl originally describes teeth spaced apart, like the petals of chrysanthemum.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p315/r13.anchor: وأصله ترتيل الأسنان وهو تفليجها كنور الأقحوان . ولما كان التقدير

BIQAI-FULL:v5p316/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p316/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p316/r1.claim: The objection and its rebuttal show the disbelievers’ hostility and desire to mislead; Biqāʿī connects this passage to the earlier description of the Garden’s people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p316/r1.anchor: واصفا لما تقدم أنه أظهره موضع الإضمار من قوله

DURR-FULL:v6p253/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p253/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p253/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the polytheists challenged Muhammad’s prophethood because revelation came a verse, two verses, or a sūra at a time rather than all at once; this passage answered them.
DURR-FULL:v6p253/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال المشركون: إن كان محمد كما يزعم نبيا فلم يعذبه ربه

DURR-FULL:v6p253/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p253/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p253/r7.claim: Qatāda says the disbelievers wanted revelation all at once, as they said it had come to Moses and Jesus.
DURR-FULL:v6p253/r7.anchor: عن قتادة {وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة} يقولون: كما أنزل على موسى وعلى عيسى

DURR-FULL:v6p253/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p253/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p253/r8.claim: Qatāda glosses tartīl as making the Qurʾān clear, with the sense of explaining it distinctly.
DURR-FULL:v6p253/r8.anchor: قال الله {كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك ورتلناه ترتيلا} قال: بيناه تبيينا

DURR-FULL:v6p254/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says revelation came one verse at a time; as the Messenger learned each verse, another came, helping him memorize the Book and steady his heart.
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك} قال: كان الله ينزل عليه الآية فإذا علمها رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v6p254/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the phrase as strengthening the Prophet’s heart and binding it firmly.
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {كذلك لنثبت} قال: لنشدد به فؤادك ونربط على قلبك

DURR-FULL:v6p254/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the Qurʾān’s tartīl as sending it in sequence, one part after another.
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {كذلك لنثبت} قال: لنشدد به فؤادك ونربط على قلبك {ورتلناه ترتيلا} قال: رسلناه ترسيلا يقول: شيئا بعد شيء

DURR-FULL:v6p254/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Quraysh asked why revelation was not sent all at once; it came little by little so each challenge could be answered with a refutation and a better explanation.
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قالت قريش ما للقرآن لم ينزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جملة واحدة

DURR-FULL:v6p254/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says verses and passages were revealed in response to questions and as replies to what people said; the revelation’s beginning and end were about twenty years apart.
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r7.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {ورتلناه ترتيلا} قال: كان ينزل عليه الآية والآيتان والآيات

DURR-FULL:v6p254/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the Qurʾān came in response to the disbelievers’ statements, teaching that God Himself answered what they said.
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r8.anchor: عن ابن جريج {كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك ورتلناه ترتيلا} قال: كان ينزل عليه القرآن جوابا لقولهم

DURR-FULL:v6p254/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r10.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r10.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī glosses the phrase as revelation sent in separate portions.
DURR-FULL:v6p254/r10.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي {ورتلناه ترتيلا} يقول: أنزل متفرقا

DURR-FULL:v6p255/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p255/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p255/r1.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the Qurʾān’s tartīl as a detailed exposition.
DURR-FULL:v6p255/r1.anchor: عن السدي {ورتلناه ترتيلا} قال: فصلنا تفصيلا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the polytheists’ challenge: if Muhammad were truly a prophet, why did his Lord not send the whole Qurʾān at once instead of a verse, two verses, or a sūra?
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال المشركون : ان كان محمد كما يزعم نبيا فلم يعذبه ربه الا ينزل عليه القران

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Qurʾān descended whole from the seventh heaven to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree and was placed at the stars; Gabriel then brought it piecemeal in response to challenges. He links its gradual descent to the Jews’ objection and the cited verses.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس : انزل الله القران جملة واحدة

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r3.claim: Qatāda reports the unbelievers’ question as asking why the Qurʾān was not revealed all at once as the revelations to Moses and Jesus were.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r3.anchor: عن قتادة : وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القران جملة واحدة كما انزل على موسى وكما انزل على عيسى

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Qurʾān was sent down on the Night of Decree and placed in Bayt al-ʿIzza.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2689/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : انزل الله القران ليلة القدر ، فجعل في بيت العزة

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, reporting Ibn ʿAbbās, glosses the challenge as «why was the Qurʾān not sent down all at once?»
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس : وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القران جملة واحدة قال : يقولون هلا انزل عليه القران جملة واحدة

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r2.claim: Al-Suddī explains the objection as asking why Muhammad did not bring the Qurʾān as Moses brought his revelation.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r2.anchor: عن السدي : وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القران جملة واحدة قال : هلا جاء به كما جاء به موسى

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the revelation strengthens and steadies Muhammad’s heart, brought by Gabriel from God; God did likewise for earlier messengers.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس : لنثبت به فؤادك يا محمد يقول : لنشدد به فؤادك ونربط على قلبك

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as sending the Qurʾān successively, one part after another.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس : قال الله عز وجل : كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك يا محمد ورتلناه ترتيلا يقول : ورسلناه ترسيلا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says verses came one, two, or several at a time in answer to questions and as rebuttals; revelation continued for about twenty years from beginning to end.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r5.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : ورتلناه ترتيلا قال : كان ينزل الاية والايتين والايات كان ينزل جوابا لهم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r6.claim: Ibrāhīm says the Qurʾān was revealed piecemeal.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r6.anchor: عن إبراهيم في قوله : ورتلناه ترتيلا قال : نزل متفرقا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r7.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the phrase as separating or detailing the Qurʾān.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r7.anchor: عن السدي ورتلناه ترتيلا يقول : فصلناه تفصيلا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r8.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as making the Qurʾān clear.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2690/r8.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : ورتلناه ترتيلا اي بيناه تبيينا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2691/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2691/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2691/r1.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd glosses the phrase as explaining the Qurʾān.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2691/r1.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد ، عن اسلم قوله : ورتلناه ترتيلا قال : فسرناه تفسيرا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2691/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2691/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2691/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God revealed a verse, then another after the Prophet learned it, teaching him the Book by heart and strengthening his heart.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2691/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك ورتلناه ترتيلا قال : كان الله عز وجل ينزل الاية عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r1.claim: The pronoun in ‘they said’ refers to the polytheists who objected to the Qur’an’s gradual descent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r1.anchor: وضمير { وقال } ظاهر في أنه عائد إلى المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r2.speaker: المشركون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r2.claim: The polytheists argued that, if the Qur’an came from God, it would have been revealed all at once.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r2.anchor: المشركون نسوا ذلك أو جهلوا فقالوا : هلا نزل القرآن على محمد جملة واحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r3.claim: Earlier scriptures were also revealed in portions: the Torah’s ten commandments, the Gospel as Jesus’s spoken sayings, and the Psalms in many parts; none was a complete book at once.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r3.anchor: جملة واحدة وإنما كانت وحيا مفرقا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r4.claim: An alternative report says Jews or Christians made the objection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r4.anchor: وقيل : إن قائل هذا اليهود أو النصارى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r5.claim: If Jews or Christians said this, it was slander, since they knew their own Torah, Gospel, and Psalms were revealed piecemeal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r5.anchor: لأنهم يعلمون أنه لم تنزل التوراة والإنجيل والزبور إلا مفرقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r6.claim: He dismisses commentators’ effort to explain the difference by contrasting Muhammad’s illiteracy with earlier prophets: none of their books descended as a complete volume.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r6.anchor: فإن تلك الكتب لم تنزل أسفارا تامة قط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r7.claim: Here نزل means أنزل and, given ‘all at once,’ does not signal the intensive or repeated sense of the verb form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r7.anchor: و { نزل } هنا مرادف أنزل وليس فيه إيذان بما يدل عليه التفعيل من التكثير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r8.claim: The response turns from the objectors to the Prophet, explaining the wisdom of gradual revelation and expressing God’s favor in strengthening and easing matters for him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p18/r8.anchor: فهو كلام مستأنف فيه رد لما أرادوه من قولهم : { لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r1.claim: كَذَٰلِكَ answers the demand for one-time revelation and points back to the gradual mode implied in their hypothetical; it stands as an accusative substitute for an absolute object, estimated as ‘We revealed it thus.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r1.anchor: فاسم الإشارة في محل نصب على أنه نائب عن مفعول مطلق جاء بدلا عن الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r2.claim: The phrase functions as a fresh turn in the dialogue, answering the objection by naming the very gradual revelation whose wisdom they missed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r2.anchor: فالتقدير : أنزلناه إنزالا كذلك الإنزال المنجم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r3.claim: The purpose lām in لِنُثَبِّتَ attaches to the implicit verb indicated by كَذَٰلِكَ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r3.anchor: واللام في { لنثبت } متعلقة بالفعل المقدر الذي دل عليه { كذلك } .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r4.claim: Tathbīt means making something firm; firmness is stability in place without wavering, and it is also figuratively certainty and assurance of good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r4.anchor: والتثبيت : جعل الشيء ثابتا . والثبات : استقرار الشيء في مكانه غير متزلزل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r5.claim: Here fuʾād means the intellect; gradual revelation makes it steady in the Qur’an’s words and meanings, without confusion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r5.anchor: والفؤاد : هنا العقل . وتثبيته بذلك الإنزال جعله ثابتا في ألفاظه ومعانيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says revelation came in portions to strengthen the Prophet’s heart so he could understand and memorize it, since learners retain knowledge better when it comes successively.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r6.anchor: فمنه ما قاله الزمخشري : الحكمة في تفريقه أن نقوي بتفريقه فؤادك حتى تعيه وتحفظه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also says revelation matched occasions, events, and questioners’ answers, making its audience more receptive and active, which reassured the Prophet and expanded his heart.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r7.anchor: أنه كان ينزل على حسب الدواعي والحوادث وجوابات السائلين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that challenging opponents with portions as each arrived made the miracle clearer and the proof stronger than one complete descent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p19/r8.anchor: إن تنزيله مفرقا وتحديهم بأن يأتوا ببعض تلك التفارق كلما نزل شيء منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r1.speaker: الجد الوزير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r1.claim: The author’s grandfather, the vizier, says gradual descent allows verses to match circumstances and suit their setting, completing their miraculous quality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r1.anchor: ومنه ما قاله الجد الوزير رحمه الله : إن القرآن لو لم ينزل منجما على حسب الحوادث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r2.claim: The author adds that gradual revelation helps memorizers understand and reflect on the Qur’an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r2.anchor: وقلت : إن نزوله منجما أعون لحفاظه على فهمه وتدبره .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r3.claim: وَرَتَّلْنَٰهُ is coordinated with كَذَٰلِكَ: God revealed it in portions and arranged it with measured order.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r3.anchor: وقوله : { ورتلناه ترتيلا } عطف على قوله { كذلك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r4.claim: Tartīl describes speech whose indications are well composed; the language authorities derive it from teeth spaced like chamomile blossoms, though they cite no Arabic poetic evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r4.anchor: واتفقت أقوال أيمة اللغة على أن هذا الترتيل مأخوذ من قولهم : ثغر مرتل ورتل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r5.claim: Tartīl may describe revelation: it arrived over time, yet each completed sūra has ordered, coherent verses, clearly articulated rather than accumulated; such coherence across time signals divine origin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r5.anchor: فإذا كمل إنزال سورة جاءت آياتها مرتبة متناسبة كأنها أنزلت جملة واحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r6.claim: Alternatively, ‘We arranged it’ means God commanded measured recitation, with no haste and with every letter and vowel articulated clearly, as in al-Muzzammil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد ب { رتلناه } أمرنا بترتيله ، أي بقراءته مرتلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r7.claim: تَرْتِيلًۭا is an accusative cognate object; its indefiniteness conveys grandeur and specifies the kind of measured arrangement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p20/r7.anchor: و { ترتيلا } مصدر منصوب على المفعول المطلق قصد به ما في التنكير من معنى التعظيم

BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r1.claim: The Mathnawi verses picture an attacker’s mockery turning back on him: one who tears others’ honor is himself exposed, then returns to Muhammad seeking pardon for ignorant ridicule.
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r1.anchor: آنكه مي دريد جامه خلق ست

BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r2.claim: Here lawla is an exhortation meaning “why not?” and tanzil is used without the sense of gradual descent, meaning “sent down,” so the wording does not contradict “all at once.”
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r2.anchor: فلولا تحضيضية بمعنى هلا والتنزيل ههنا مجرد عن معنى التدريج بمعنى أنزل كخبر بمعنى أخبر

BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r3.claim: The unbelievers ask for a single, simultaneous revelation, like the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms.

BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r4.claim: Their objection is bewildered and empty: inimitability is unaffected by gradual or complete revelation; they had been challenged to produce one sura and failed despite risking wealth and lives.
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r4.anchor: وهذا اعتراض حيرة وبهت لا طائل تحته لأن الإعجاز لا يختلف بنزوله جملة أو مفرقا وقد تحدوا بسورة واحدة فعجزوا

BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r5.claim: Kadhalika is accusative as an adjective of an emphasized verbal noun, with the following clause giving its cause; it points back to the divided revelation they criticized.
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r5.anchor: محل الكاف النصب على أنها صفة لمصدر مؤكد معلل بما بعده وذلك إشارة إلى ما يفهم من كلامهم

BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r6.claim: Gradual revelation strengthens Muhammad’s heart by easing memorization, understanding, grasping rulings, and acting on them; each new revelation for an event increases strength and insight.
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r6.anchor: لنقوي بذلك التنزيل المفرق فؤادك أي قلبك فإن فيه تيسيرا لحفظ النظم وفهم المعنى وضبط الأحكام والعمل بها

BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r7.claim: A single bulk revelation made obedience difficult for the Israelites when the Torah descended all at once.
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r7.anchor: ألا ترى أن التوراة أنزلت دفعة فشق العمل على بني إسرائيل

BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r8.claim: The Qur’an’s gradual descent, a privilege particular to Muhammad among the prophets, lets his luminous heart take on the Qur’an’s character, grow strong in its light, and be nourished by its truths and knowledge.
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r8.anchor: وبالجملة إنزال القرآن منجما فضيلة خص بها نبينا عليه السلام من بين سائر النبيين فإن المقصود من إنزاله أن يتخلق قلبه المنير بخلق القرآن

BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r9.claim: Rain spread over time nourishes crops better than a single downpour, illustrating why the Qur’an’s benefits are fulfilled through gradual revelation.
BURSEVI:v6p151#2/r9.anchor: ألا يرى أن الماء لو نزل من السماء جملة واحدة لما كانت تربية الزروع به مثلها إذا نزل مفرقا

BURSEVI:v6p152/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p152/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p152/r1.claim: “We recited it distinctly” is coordinated with an elided verb expressing “We sent it down.”
BURSEVI:v6p152/r1.anchor: ورتلناه ترتيلا} عطف على ذلك المضمر

BURSEVI:v6p152/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p152/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p152/r2.claim: Tartil means separating and placing each word after the last with a slight pause without cutting breath; its root image is the spacing of teeth.
BURSEVI:v6p152/r2.anchor: والترتيل التفريق ومجيء الكلمة بعد الأخرى بسكوت يسير دون قطع النفس وأصله في الأسنان وهو تفريجها

BURSEVI:v6p152/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p152/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p152/r3.claim: God sent and recited it to Muhammad gradually, with calm and deliberation, over twenty or twenty-three years.
BURSEVI:v6p152/r3.anchor: كذلك نزلناه وقرأناه عليك شيئا بعد شيء على تؤدة وتمهل في عشرين سنة أو ثلاث وعشرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others report Quraysh's challenge: if the Qurʾān came from God, it should have descended all at once like the Torah and Gospel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس وغيره أن كفار قريش قالوا في بعض معارضتهم لو كان هذا القرآن من عند الله لنزل جملة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r2.claim: One interpretation makes “thus” part of the unbelievers' statement, pointing to the Torah and Gospel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r2.anchor: وقوله كذلك يحتمل أن يكون من قول الكفار إشارة إلى التوراة والإنجيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r3.claim: Preferably, “thus” begins God's response: He intended the Qurʾān to descend in portions to strengthen Muhammad's heart and help him retain it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون من الكلام المستأنف وهو أولى ومعناه كما نزل أردناه فالإشارة إلى نزوله متفرقة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r4.speaker: مكي والرماني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r4.claim: Makkī and al-Rummānī say gradual revelation suited Muhammad's illiteracy, matched timed events, and extended over more than twenty years; other messengers could write and received revelation all at once.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r4.anchor: وقال مكي والرماني من حيث كان أميا لا يكتب وليطابق الأسباب المؤقتة فنزل في نيف على عشرين سنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r5.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd reads “li-yuthabbita” with yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن مسعود «ليثبت» بالياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r6.claim: Tartīl means separating or spacing what is sequential; it also describes even teeth and measured recitation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r6.anchor: والترتيل التفريق بين الشيء المتتابع ومنه قولهم ثغر رتل ومنه ترتيل القراءة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r7.claim: God intended revelation to accompany the incidents and events whose timing He had decreed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p209#2/r7.anchor: وأراد الله تعالى أن ينزل القرآن في النوازل والحوادث التي قدرها وقدر نزوله فيها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p88#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p88#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p88#2/r1.claim: The critics wanted the Quran sent down all at once, as the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms were; God says it was sent gradually.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p88#2/r1.anchor: أي كما أنزلت التوراة والإنجيل والزبور فقال الله عز وجل كذلك أي أنزلناه كذلك متفرقا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p88#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p88#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p88#2/r2.claim: Its staged revelation strengthens the Prophet's heart and increases insight because it came in response to each event, making him less lonely.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p88#2/r2.anchor: وذلك أنه كان يأتيه الوحي في كل أمر وحادثة فكان أقوى لقلبه وأنور لبصيرته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p88#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p88#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p88#2/r3.claim: The Quran was sent in tartīl: deliberate, measured delivery rather than haste.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p88#2/r3.anchor: ورتلناه ترتيلا أي أنزلناه على الترتيل وهو التمكث الذي يضاد العجلة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r1.speaker: الذين كفروا
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r1.claim: The unbelievers objected that the Quran should have been sent down all at once, like the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and other revealed books.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r1.anchor: عن كثرة اعتراض الكفار وتعنتهم، وكلامهم فيما لا يعنيهم، حيث قالوا: {لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r2.claim: God answered that revelation came in stages over twenty-three years, in response to events and needs for rulings, to strengthen believers’ hearts; see 17:106.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r2.anchor: إنما أنزل منجما في ثلاث وعشرين سنة بحسب الوقائع والحوادث، وما يحتاج إليه من الأحكام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r3.claim: Qatada explains tartīl as making the Quran clear, clarity upon clarity.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r4.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam explains tartīl as expounding or interpreting the Quran.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: وفسرناه تفسيرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r7.claim: The frequent revelation morning and evening, day and night, in travel and at home honors the Messenger; receiving each installment is a higher station than that of the other prophets.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r7.anchor: كان يأتيه الوحي من الله بالقرآن صباحا ومساء، ليلا ونهارا، سفرا وحضرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r8.claim: The Quran is God’s most noble revealed book, and Muhammad is His greatest prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r8.anchor: فالقرآن أشرف كتاب أنزله الله، ومحمد، صلوات الله وسلامه عليه، أعظم نبي أرسله الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Quran descended all at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of Power, then came down over twenty years; Ibn Kathir cites al-Nasai and 17:106.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p109#2/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أنزل القرآن جملة إلى سماء الدنيا في ليلة القدر، ثم نزل بعد ذلك في عشرين سنة

JISHUMI:v7p5295/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5295/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5295/r5.claim: Tartīl is clear recitation; the source also describes spaced teeth and white, moist teeth.
JISHUMI:v7p5295/r5.anchor: والترتيل: التبيين، رتل القرآن: بين [قراءته]، وثغر رتل، ورتل بفتح التاء وسكونها: إذا كان مفلجا لا لصص فيه،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r1.claim: Nuzzila here means anzala; otherwise the wording would be strained.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r1.anchor: { نزل } ههنا بمعنى أنزل لا غير ، كخبر بمعنى أخبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r2.claim: The demand for one-piece revelation is an objection showing their flight from truth and refusal to follow it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r2.anchor: وهذا أيضا من اعتراضاتهم واقتراحاتهم الدالة على شرادهم عن الحق وتجافيهم عن اتباعه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r3.speaker: author
