KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r3.claim: Zamakhsharī identifies the objectors as Quraysh.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r4.claim: An alternative identification says the objectors were Jews.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r5.claim: They ask why the Qurʾān was not sent down at once, like the three earlier scriptures, instead of in portions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r5.anchor: قالوا : هلا أنزل عليه دفعة واحدة في وقت واحد كما أنزلت الكتب الثلاثة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r6.claim: The objection is pointless because the Qurʾān’s inimitability and force as proof do not differ whether it came all at once or in parts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r6.anchor: وهذا فضول من القول ومماراة بما لا طائل تحته ؛ لأن أمر الإعجاز والاحتجاج به لا يختلف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r7.claim: The answer is that it was sent down in portions; gradual revelation strengthens the Prophet’s heart so he can comprehend and memorize it piece by piece.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r7.anchor: وقوله : { كذالك } جواب لهم ، أي : كذلك أنزل مفرقا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r8.claim: The Prophet needed gradual reception because, unlike Moses, David, and Jesus, he was unlettered and could not read or write.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r8.anchor: والرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم فارقت حاله حال موسى وداود وعيسى عليهم السلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r9.claim: The Qurʾān was revealed gradually over twenty years; another report gives twenty-three years.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r9.anchor: فأنزل عليه منجما في عشرين سنة . وقيل : في ثلاث وعشرين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r10.claim: Gradual revelation also matched events and answers to questioners, and allowed abrogating and abrogated passages, which requires piecemeal revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r10.anchor: وأيضا : فكان ينزل على حسب الحوادث وجوابات السائلين ، ولأن بعضه منسوخ وبعضه ناسخ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r11.claim: Although dhālika appears to point back to the demand for one-piece revelation, that demand implies asking why it was not revealed in parts, so the answer means it was.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r11.anchor: فإن قلت : ذلك في كذلك يجب أن يكون إشارة إلى شيء تقدمه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r12.claim: Their inability to produce even one short sūra, followed by resort to confrontation and war, exposes their failed challenge; asking for the whole assumes they could meet it in parts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r12.anchor: والدليل على فساد هذا الاعتراض : أنهم عجزوا عن أن يأتوا بنجم واحد من نجومه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r13.claim: Rattalnāhu may coordinate with the verb governing dhālika, so the sense is that God divided and ordered the revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r13.anchor: ورتلناه } معطوف على الفعل الذي تعلق به كذلك ، كأنه قال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r14.claim: Alternatively, it means God commanded measured recitation, as in 73:4.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283/r14.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى : وأمرنا بترتيل قراءته ، وذلك قوله :

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283#2/r1.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283#2/r1.claim: A report attributed in the preceding passage to ʿĀʾisha describes the Prophet’s measured recitation: unlike rapid reading, a listener could count its letters; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283#2/r1.anchor: ( 774 ) ( لا كسردكم هذا ، لو أراد السامع أن يعد حروفه يعدها )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283#2/r2.claim: The root image of tartīl is the even spacing of teeth, whose whiteness is likened to chamomile.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283#2/r2.anchor: وأصله : الترتيل في الأسنان : وهو تفليجها . يقال : ثغر رتل ومرتل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283#2/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283#2/r3.claim: Another explanation is that revelation was spaced out over twenty years rather than delivered in closely spaced installments.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p283#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : هو أن نزله مع كونه متفرقا على تمكث وتمهل في مدة متباعدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the unbelievers who demanded one complete revelation were Quraysh.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم كفار قريش , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r2.claim: A second view identifies them as Jews who saw the Qurʾan revealed in portions and asked why it was not sent all at once as the Torah was to Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنهم اليهود حين رأوا نزول القرآن مفرقا , قالوا : هلا أنزل عليه جملة واحدة , كما أنزلت التوراة على موسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the Qurʾan steadies the Prophet by encouraging his heart, since its miraculous character proves his truthfulness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما : لنشجع به قلبك , لأنه معجز يدل على صدقك , وهو معنى قول السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, God revealed the Qurʾan in portions in order to steady the Prophet's heart.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r4.anchor: الثاني : معناه كذلك أنزلناه مفرقا لنثبته في فؤادك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r5.claim: One explanation for gradual revelation is that the Prophet was unlettered and the Qurʾan was not sent down as a written book, so portions fixed it firmly in his heart.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما : لأنه كان أميا ولم ينزل القرآن عليه مكتوبا , فكان نزوله مفرقا أثبت في فؤاده , وأعلق بقلبه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r6.claim: Another explanation is that continual revelation prevented the Prophet from feeling lonely during pauses in revelation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r6.anchor: الثاني : لنثبت فؤادك باتصال الوحي ومداومة نزول القرآن ، فلا تصير بانقطاع الوحي مستوحشا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets tartil as sending the Qurʾan gradually, one part after another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r7.anchor: أحدها : ورسلناه ترسيلا ، شيئا بعد شيء ، قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r8.speaker: إبراهيم
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r8.claim: Ibrahim interprets tartil as dividing the Qurʾan into portions.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r9.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r9.claim: Al-Suddi interprets tartil as setting out the Qurʾan distinctly.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets tartil as explaining the Qurʾan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r10.anchor: الرابع : وفسرناه تفسيرا ، قاله ابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r11.claim: Qatada interprets tartil as clarifying the Qurʾan.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet's instruction to recite with tartil: make it clear, do not chop it like dry dates or rush like poetry, and do not focus only on reaching the sura's end.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p143#2/r12.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( يا ابن عباس إذا قرأت القرآن فرتله ترتيلا )

MUQATIL:25:32-34/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:32-34/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:32-34/r1.claim: The unbelievers objected that the Qur'an should have been sent down all at once, as they said it was with Moses and Jesus.
MUQATIL:25:32-34/r1.anchor: وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل } يعنى هلا نزل { عليه القرآن جملة واحدة

MUQATIL:25:32-34/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:32-34/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:32-34/r2.claim: Its gradual revelation was meant to make the Qur'an firm in Muhammad's heart.
MUQATIL:25:32-34/r2.anchor: كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك } يعنى ليثبت القرآن فى قلبك { ورتلناه ترتيلا

MUQATIL:25:32-34/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:32-34/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:32-34/r3.claim: God sent it down gradually, verse after verse.
MUQATIL:25:32-34/r3.anchor: ورتلناه ترتيلا } [آية: 32] يعنى نرسله ترسلا آيات، ثم آيات،

MUQATIL:25:32-34/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:32-34/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:32-34/r4.claim: Muqatil links the gradual revelation to the statement that the Qur'an was divided for recitation over time.
MUQATIL:25:32-34/r4.anchor: وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r1.claim: The disbelievers objecting here are identified as Quraysh or the Jews.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r2.claim: The phrase is a circumstantial qualifier of the Quran and means all together.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r3.claim: The objection is empty disputation because the Quran's inimitability is unaffected by gradual or single-time revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r3.anchor: فضول من القول ومماراة بما لا طائل تحته لأن أمر الاعجاز الاحتجاج به لا يختلف بنزوله جملة واحدة أو متفرقا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r4.claim: The opponents failed the challenge to produce even the shortest surah, then resorted to battle and arguments.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r4.anchor: تحدوا بالاتيان بسورة واحدة من أصغر السور فابرزوا صفحة عجزهم حتى لا ذوا بالمناصبة وفرعوا إلى المحاربة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r5.claim: Nuzzila here means anzala, sent down; otherwise it would contradict the phrase all at once.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r5.anchor: ونزل هنا بمعنى أنزل وإلا لكان متدافعا بدليل جملة واحدة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r6.claim: The answer is that the Quran came in parts over twenty or twenty-three years; likewise points back to their request for one revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r6.anchor: أى كذلك أنزل مفرقا فى عشرين سنة أو فى ثلاث وعشرين وذلك فى كذلك اشارة إلى مدلول قوله لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r7.claim: Gradual revelation steadies the Prophet's heart and aids memorization, since learning bit by bit is manageable while receiving all at once would overwhelm him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r7.anchor: حتى تعيه ونحفظه لأن المتلقن إنما يقوى قلبه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r8.claim: Alternatively, successive revelations soothe the Prophet's heart like repeated letters from a beloved.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r8.anchor: أو لنثبت به فؤادك عن الضجر بتواتر الوصول وتتابع الرسول لأن قلب المحب يسكن بتواصل كتب المحبوب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r9.claim: Coordinated with the verb implied in likewise, the phrase means that God separated the Quran and made it clear in measured delivery.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p167#4/r9.anchor: معطوف على الفعل الذى تعلق به كذلك كأنه قال كذلك فرقناه ورتلناه أى اقرأه بترسل وتثبت أو بيناه تبيينا

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās attributes the demand for one-time revelation to the Quraysh unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r1.anchor: اختلف في قائل ذلك على قولين: أحدهما: أنهم كفار قريش قاله ابن عباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r2.speaker: اليهود
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r2.claim: Another view attributes the demand to Jews, who compared the Qurʾān's gradual descent with the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r2.anchor: الثاني: أنهم اليهود حين رأوا نزول القرآن مفرقا قالوا: هلا أنزل عليه جملة واحدة كما أنزلت التوراة على موسى والإنجيل على عيسى والزبور على داود.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r3.claim: God revealed it gradually to strengthen the Prophet's heart so he could retain and bear the revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r3.anchor: فقال الله تعالى: { كذلك } أي فعلنا { لنثبت به فؤادك } نقوي به قلبك فتعيه وتحمله

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r4.claim: Earlier scriptures went to prophets who could read and write, whereas the Qurʾān was sent to an unlettered prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r4.anchor: لأن الكتب المتقدمة أنزلت على أنبياء يكتبون ويقرؤون، والقرآن أنزل على نبي أمي

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r5.claim: The Qurʾān includes abrogating and abrogated rulings and answers to questions, so its portions came as circumstances required.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r5.anchor: ولأن من القرآن الناسخ والمنسوخ، ومنه ما هو جواب لمن سأل عن أمور، ففرقناه

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r6.claim: Gradual revelation made the Qurʾān easier for the Prophet to retain and for people to practice; each new revelation strengthened his heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r6.anchor: ليكون أوعى للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأيسر على العامل به فكان كلما نزل وحي جديد زاده قوة قلب.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r7.claim: God could have taught the whole Book and Qurʾān in one instant, but chose otherwise; no one may object to His wisdom.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r7.anchor: في قدرة الله أن يعلمه الكتاب والقرآن في لحظة واحدة، ولكنه لم يفعل ولا معترض عليه في حكمه،

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r8.claim: One construal makes kathālika the end of the unbelievers' statement, comparing it with the Torah and Gospel, then begins God's answer at li-nuthabbita.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r8.anchor: وقد قيل: إن قوله { كذلك } من كلام المشركين، أي لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة كذلك، أي كالتوراة والإنجيل، فيتم الوقف على { كذلك } ثم يبتدىء { لنثبت به فوادك }.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r9.claim: Another construal pauses after jumlatan wāḥidatan, then reads kathālika as God's explanation that He sent it gradually to strengthen the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r9.anchor: ثم يبتدىء { كذلك لنثبت به فوادك }

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r10.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī judges the first stopping and speech arrangement better, though the second also comes in transmitted interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r10.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: والوجه الأول أجود وأحسن، والقول الثاني قد جاء به التفسير،

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Qurʾān descended from the Preserved Tablet to the heavenly scribes, who sent it in stages to Gabriel over twenty nights; Gabriel then delivered it gradually to Muḥammad over twenty years.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33/r11.anchor:
عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى:
إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر
[القدر: 1] قال: أنزل القرآن جملة واحدة

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r1.claim: Qurṭubī continues Ibn ʿAbbās's report, reading the stars as portions of the Qurʾān.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r1.anchor:
يعني نجوم القرآن
وإنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r2.claim: Rattalnāhu means God sent the Qurʾān gradually, one portion after another.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r2.anchor: { ورتلناه ترتيلا } يقول: ورسلناه ترسيلا يقول: شيئا بعد شيء.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r5.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r5.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says gradual revelation spared people the burden of receiving all obligations at once and repeatedly alerted them; God knew gradual descent was beneficial.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r5.anchor: ولو نزل جملة بما فيه من الفرائض لثقل عليهم، وعلم الله عز وجل أن الصلاح في إنزاله متفرقا، لأنهم ينبهون به مرة بعد مرة

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r6.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r6.claim: Al-Naḥḥās argues that gradual revelation lets rulings apply until later abrogation; one-time revelation could not present both commands together.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r6.anchor: وفيه ناسخ ومنسوخ، فكانوا يتعبدون بالشيء إلى وقت بعينه قد علم الله عز وجل فيه الصلاح، ثم ينزل النسخ بعد ذلك فمحال أن ينزل جملة واحدة: افعلوا كذا ولا تفعلوا.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r7.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r7.claim: Al-Naḥḥās prefers ending the sentence at jumlatan wāḥidatan; pausing at kathālika would imply comparison with earlier scriptures not yet mentioned.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:32-33#2/r7.anchor: قال النحاس: والأولى أن يكون التمام { جملة واحدة } لأنه إذا وقف على { كذلك } صار المعنى كالتوراة والإنجيل والزبور ولم يتقدم لها ذكر.

QASHANI:25:27-32/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:27-32/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:27-32/r1.claim: After returning from annihilation to subsistence to guide creation, the Prophet's heart is veiled, and his self appears through its attributes at intervals, producing spiritual variegation.
QASHANI:25:27-32/r1.anchor: لما رد في مقام البقاء بعد الفناء إلى حجاب القلب لهداية الخلق كان قد يظهر نفسه وقتا غب وقت على قلبه بصفاتها، ويحدث له التلوين بسببها

QASHANI:25:27-32/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:27-32/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:27-32/r2.claim: God repeatedly restores and disciplines the Prophet through revelation and spiritual attraction, admonishing him so he returns and repents in every state until firmly established.
QASHANI:25:27-32/r2.anchor: فكان يتداركه الله تعالى بإنزال الوحي والجذبة ويؤدبه ويعاتبه فيرجع إليه في كل حال ويتوب

QASHANI:25:27-32/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:27-32/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:25:27-32/r3.claim: The Prophet says his Lord educated him and perfected his education.
QASHANI:25:27-32/r3.anchor: قال عليه السلام: " أدبني ربي فأحسن تأديبي "

QASHANI:25:27-32/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:27-32/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:25:27-32/r4.claim: The Prophet reports a recurring clouding of his heart and says he seeks God's forgiveness seventy times each day.
QASHANI:25:27-32/r4.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إنه ليغان على قلبي وإني لأستغفر الله في اليوم سبعين مرة "

QASHANI:25:27-32/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:27-32/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:27-32/r5.claim: The prophetic trial arose through the call, which exposed him to people's harm, enmity, and opposition.
QASHANI:25:27-32/r5.anchor: وكان سبب ظهور ابتلاء الله تعالى إياه بالدعوة لإيذاء الناس إياه وعداوتهم ومناصبتهم له

QASHANI:25:27-32/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:27-32/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:27-32/r6.claim: One wisdom of the trial is the Prophet's own perfection: facing enemies of varied natures teaches him the wisdom and virtue of every attribute, bringing together the noble traits and perfections of all prophets.
QASHANI:25:27-32/r6.anchor: فيؤدبه الله بحكمة وجود كل صفة وفضيلة كل قوة، فيحصل له جميع مكارم الأخلاق وكمالات جميع الأنبياء

QASHANI:25:27-32/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:27-32/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:27-32/r7.claim: The heart's differing aspects, arising through the soul's attributes, make it receptive to diverse wisdoms and virtues as its orientation becomes particular to each.
QASHANI:25:27-32/r7.anchor: لولا الجهات المختلفة في القلب بواسطة صفات النفس لما استعد لقبول الحكم المتفننة والفضائل بتخصص توجهه لكل واحدة منها

QASHANI:25:27-32/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:27-32/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:27-32/r8.claim: A second wisdom is for the community: as messenger to people of diverse capacities, he needs comprehensive wisdom, virtues, and morals to guide, purify, and teach each according to their aptitude.
QASHANI:25:27-32/r8.anchor: فإنه رسول إلى الكل واستعداداتهم متباينة، ونفوسهم في الصفات متفاوتة. فيجب أن يكون فيه جوامع الحكم والكلم والفضائل والأخلاق

QASHANI:25:27-32/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:27-32/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:27-32/r9.claim: The Qur'an's gradual descent matches the changing emergence of the Prophet's attributes over time and steadies him in the complete path toward, with, and from God; he is a model for seekers, realized ones, and those who perfect others.
QASHANI:25:27-32/r9.anchor: كون التنزيل مفرقا منجما إنما يكون بحسب اختلاف صفات نفسه في الظهور منها على أوقاته موجبا لتثبت قلبه في الاستقامة في السلوك إلى الله، وفي الله عند الاتصاف بصفاته، ومن الله في هداية الخلق

QASHANI:25:27-32#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:27-32#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:27-32#2/r1.claim: Tartil means spacing each portion of revelation from the next long enough for it to settle firmly in the heart and become a stable disposition rather than a passing state.
QASHANI:25:27-32#2/r1.anchor: والترتيل هو أن يتخلل بين كل نجم وآخر مدة يمكن فيها تزايله في قلبه ويترسخ ويصير ملكة لا حالا

RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r1.speaker: الذين كفروا
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r1.claim: The Meccans objected that Muhammad claimed prophethood but the Qur’an was not sent all at once, as the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms were.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r1.anchor: اعلم أن هذا هو الشبهة الخامسة لمنكري نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says there were twenty-two or twenty-three years between the beginning and end of revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r2.anchor: وعن ابن جريج بين أوله وآخره اثنتان أو ثلاث وعشرون سنة

RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r3.claim: Because Muhammad could neither read nor write, receiving the Qur’an all at once could have exceeded his ability to retain it and exposed him to mistakes or forgetfulness; the Torah was written for Moses to read.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r3.anchor: لم يكن من أهل القراءة والكتابة فلو نزل عليه ذلك جملة واحدة كان لا يضبطه

RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r4.claim: Gradual revelation prevents dependence on a written copy and lax memorization, making Muhammad’s retention more complete and his effort greater.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r4.anchor: فالله تعالى ما أعطاه الكتاب دفعة واحدة بل كان ينزل عليه وظيفة ليكون حفظه له أكمل

RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r5.claim: Had all scripture descended at once, all laws would have burdened people simultaneously; gradual legislation made compliance easier.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r5.anchor: لو أنزل الكتاب جملة واحدة على الخلق لنزلت الشرائع بأسرها دفعة واحدة على الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r6.claim: Seeing Gabriel repeatedly strengthened Muhammad to convey revelation, bear prophetic trials and harm from his people, and wage jihad.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r6.anchor: إذا شاهد جبريل حالا بعد حال يقوى قلبه بمشاهدته

RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r7.claim: Its piecemeal descent still establishes its miraculousness: if humans could produce its like, they could match it in piecemeal form.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r7.anchor: لما تم شرط الإعجاز فيه مع كونه منجما ثبت كونه معجزا

RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r8.claim: Revelation responded to questions and events, increasing insight by joining eloquence with reports of the unseen.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r8.anchor: كان القرآن ينزل بحسب أسئلتهم والوقائع الواقعة لهم فكانوا يزدادون بصيرة

RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r9.claim: Since Muhammad challenged them from the start with each newly revealed portion, their inability to match any portion established their inability to match the whole.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r9.anchor: كان يتحداهم من أول الأمر فكأنه تحداهم بكل واحد من نجوم القرآن فلما عجزوا عنه

RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r10.claim: Gradual revelation preserved Gabriel’s exalted role as envoy between God and the prophets, carrying God’s message to people.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69/r10.anchor: السفارة بين الله تعالى وبين أنبيائه وتبليغ كلامه إلى الخلق منصب عظيم

RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r1.claim: One reading makes “thus” complete the polytheists’ statement: they wanted a single revelation like the Torah and Gospel, with no omitted words.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r1.anchor: أنه من تمام كلام المشركين أي جملة واحدة كذلك أي كالتوراة والإنجيل

RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, “thus” begins God’s answer: He sent the Qur’an down in portions to strengthen Muhammad’s heart.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r2.anchor: أنه كلام الله تعالى ذكره جوابا لهم أي كذلك أنزلناه مفرقا

RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r3.claim: Although a demonstrative normally points to something preceding, the objection’s demand for one-time revelation implies a complaint about piecemeal descent, which is what “thus” refers to.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r3.anchor: معناه لم نزل مفرقا فذلك إشارة إليه

RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r4.claim: Tartīl in speech means that its parts follow deliberately and at an unhurried pace; the word originally describes gaps between teeth, opposite tightly aligned teeth.
RAZI-FULL:v24p69#2/r4.anchor: معنى الترتيل في الكلام أن يأتي بعضه على أثر بعض على تؤدة وتمهل

STUDYQURAN:25:32/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r1.claim: The Quran was revealed across the Prophet's mission over twenty-two or twenty-three years.
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r1.anchor: The Quran was revealed over the course of the Prophet’s entire mission of twenty-two or twenty-three years

STUDYQURAN:25:32/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r2.claim: The promise to strengthen the Prophet's heart echoes 11:120, which says accounts of earlier messengers strengthen it.
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r2.anchor: The message of this verse is connected with 11:120: All that We recount unto thee of the stories of the messengers is that whereby We make firm thine heart

STUDYQURAN:25:32/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r3.speaker: IK and Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r3.claim: Some understand the measured recitation to mean that God explained the Quran's interpretation to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r3.anchor: Some understand We have recited it unto thee in a measured pace to mean, “We have explained to thee its interpretation”

STUDYQURAN:25:32/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r4.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r4.claim: Gradual revelation tracked the Prophet's life, legislated commands and prohibitions over time, helped establish the community, and supported him in struggles with enemies.
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r4.anchor: the relationship of the Quran to the events of the life of the Prophet, the gradual legislation of commands and prohibitions

STUDYQURAN:25:32/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r5.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī lists benefits of successive revelation: gradual legislation, learning and memorizing in portions, and responses suited to believers' questions and circumstances.
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r5.anchor: Al-Rāzī understands the gradual application of the commands and prohibitions, the memorization and understanding of one part at a time

STUDYQURAN:25:32/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r6.claim: The divided recitation also connects to 17:106, which describes reciting the Quran to people in intervals through successive revelation.
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r6.anchor: see also commentary on 17:106: And [We sent it down] as a recitation We have divided in parts

STUDYQURAN:25:32/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r7.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r7.claim: Some say the Quran first descended all at once from the Preserved Tablet or Mother of the Book to the lowest heaven, then descended gradually to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:25:32/r7.anchor: some commentators describe how the Quran descended all at once from the Preserved Tablet (85:22) or Mother of the Book (13:39)

TAB-FULL:v17p445/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p445/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p445/r1.claim: The unbelievers asked why the Qur'an was not sent to Muhammad all at once, as the Torah had been sent to Moses.
TAB-FULL:v17p445/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة، كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك ورتلناه ترتيلا} [الفرقان: 32] قال:

TAB-FULL:v17p445/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p445/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p445/r2.claim: God sent the Qur'an down verse by verse and piece by piece to strengthen the Prophet's heart.
TAB-FULL:v17p445/r2.anchor: قال الله: {كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك} [الفرقان: 32] تنزيله عليك الآية بعد الآية والشيء بعد الشيء لنثبت به فؤادك

TAB-FULL:v17p445/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p445/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p445/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says each verse was revealed and learned before another came, teaching the Prophet the Book by heart and strengthening him.
TAB-FULL:v17p445/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة، كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك ورتلناه ترتيلا} [الفرقان: 32] قال:

TAB-FULL:v17p445/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p445/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v17p445/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the Qur'an came in response to the unbelievers, showing Muhammad that God answered them truthfully and bolstering his resolve and certainty.
TAB-FULL:v17p445/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: {وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة} [الفرقان: 32]

TAB-FULL:v17p447/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r1.claim: God taught the Qur'an to the Prophet piece by piece until he memorized it.
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم، في قوله: {ورتلناه ترتيلا} [الفرقان: 32] قال: «نزل متفرقا»

TAB-FULL:v17p447/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r2.claim: In recitation, tartil means reading deliberately and carefully.
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ورتلناه ترتيلا} [الفرقان: 32] قال: " فسرناه تفسيرا

TAB-FULL:v17p447/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r3.claim: Ibrahim interprets the phrase as the Qur'an having been revealed in separate portions.
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r3.anchor: عن إبراهيم، في قوله: {ورتلناه ترتيلا} [الفرقان: 32] قال: «نزل متفرقا»

TAB-FULL:v17p447/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says one, two, or several verses came in response to questions, answering and refuting the Prophet's opponents; revelation spanned about twenty years.
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r4.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {ورتلناه ترتيلا} [الفرقان: 32] قال: «كان ينزل آية وآيتين وآيات جوابا لهم،

TAB-FULL:v17p447/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that revelation began when the Prophet was forty and that he died aged sixty-two or sixty-three.
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: {ورتلناه ترتيلا} [الفرقان: 32] قال: «كان بين ما أنزل القرآن إلى آخره أنزل عليه لأربعين،

TAB-FULL:v17p447/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets tartil as explanation and cites the command to recite the Qur'an with tartil.
TAB-FULL:v17p447/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ورتلناه ترتيلا} [الفرقان: 32] قال: " فسرناه تفسيرا

TABATABAI:25:32/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32/r1.claim: The objectors are Arab polytheists resisting the Qur’an’s call, repeating their earlier charge that it was fabricated.
TABATABAI:25:32/r1.anchor: المراد بهم مشركو العرب الرادون لدعوة القرآن كما في قدحهم السابق

TABATABAI:25:32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32/r2.claim: As explained earlier, inzāl indicates sending down at once, while tanzīl indicates gradual descent.
TABATABAI:25:32/r2.anchor: تقدم أن الإنزال والتنزيل إنما يفترقان في أن الإنزال يفيد الدفعة والتنزيل يفيد التدريج

TABATABAI:25:32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:25:32/r3.claim: Some say tanzīl here loses its gradual sense because gradual division conflicts with “all together”; the request means sending it down all at once, like earlier scriptures.
TABATABAI:25:32/r3.anchor: ذكر بعضهم أن التنزيل في هذه الآية منسلخ عن معنى التدريج

TABATABAI:25:32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32/r4.claim: The Torah apparently came as a written book on tablets, whereas the Qur’an was received orally from Gabriel; receiving a recitation necessarily proceeds from beginning to end, without excluding gradual parts.
TABATABAI:25:32/r4.anchor: والقرآن إنما كان ينزل عليه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بالتلقي من عند الله بتوسط الروح الأمين

TABATABAI:25:32/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32/r5.claim: The Arabs proposed that Gabriel recite all the Qur’an at one time and Muhammad receive it at once, even if recitation and reception took time; this reading fits gradual tanzīl.
TABATABAI:25:32/r5.anchor: فكان اقتراحهم أن الذي يتلوه ملك الوحي على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سورة بعد سورة وآية بعد آية

TABATABAI:25:32/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32/r6.claim: Nothing in their words shows they wanted a written book delivered at once like the Torah, Gospel, or Psalms; they did not even believe in those scriptures.
TABATABAI:25:32/r6.anchor: فلا دلالة في الكلام المنقول عنهم على ذلك. على أنهم ما كانوا مؤمنين بهذه الكتب السماوية

TABATABAI:25:32/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32/r7.claim: Their objection implies that a divine religious book should present a complete, ordered religion, but the Qur’an comes in portions tied to separate events, so they call its claimant an inventor.
TABATABAI:25:32/r7.anchor: فقولهم { لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة } اعتراض منهم على القرآن من جهة نحو نزوله

TABATABAI:25:32-33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r1.claim: The objectors say the Qur’an is scattered speech attached to successive events, which its claimant invents and falsely attributes to God, making him a misguided apostate.
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r1.anchor: وليس كذلك بل هو أقوال متفرقة يأتي بها في وقائع مختلفة وحوادث متشتتة

TABATABAI:25:32-33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r2.claim: Thabāt is the opposite of disappearance; ithbāt and tathbīt share the sense of establishing, with a difference of one-time versus gradual action.
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r2.anchor: الثبات ضد الزوال، والإثبات والتثبيت بمعنى واحد

TABATABAI:25:32-33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r3.claim: Fu’ād means the heart, understood in al-Mīzān’s recurring usage as the human being’s perceiving self.
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r3.anchor: والفؤاد القلب والمراد به كما مر غير مرة الأمر المدرك من الإنسان وهو نفسه

TABATABAI:25:32-33/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r4.speaker: قالوا
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r4.claim: Lexicographers explain tartīl as orderly delivery, one thing following another.
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r4.anchor: كما قالوا - الترسيل والإتيان بالشيء عقيب الشيء

TABATABAI:25:32-33/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r6.claim: The author takes kādhalika with an omitted verb, taqdīruhu nazzalnāhu, and rejects the view that it completes the unbelievers’ statement as very feeble.
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r6.anchor: وظاهر السياق أن قوله { كذلك } متعلق بفعل مقدر

TABATABAI:25:32-33/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r7.claim: Sequential instruction first stores knowledge, but it becomes settled and effective when need arises and the learner applies it; the doctor teaching beside a patient illustrates this.
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r7.anchor: وأما استقرارها في النفس بحيث تنمو النفس عليها وتترتب عليها آثارها المطلوبة منها فيحتاج إلى مسيس الحاجة والإشراف على العمل

TABATABAI:25:32-33/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r8.claim: Teaching when need and action are present roots knowledge more firmly, especially truths guided by human nature, which is ready to accept them when it feels the need.
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r8.anchor: إلقاء أي نظرة علمية عند مسيس الحاجة وحضور وقت العمل إلى من يراد تعليمه وتربيته أثبت في النفس

TABATABAI:25:32-33/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r9.claim: Islamic teachings are practical individual and social laws for human flourishing, grounded in virtue and universal divine truths culminating in tawḥīd and then moral and practical duties.
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r9.anchor: شرائع وأحكام عملية وقوانين فردية واجتماعية تسعد الحياة الإنسانية مبنية على الأخلاق الفاضلة المرتبطة بالمعارف الكلية الإلهية

TABATABAI:25:32-33/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r10.claim: The best education unfolds these truths with events and needs, connecting right belief, virtue, lawful practice, lessons from earlier peoples, and the fate of transgressors and tyrants.
TABATABAI:25:32-33/r10.anchor: فأحسن التعليم وأكمل التربية أن تلقى هذه المعارف العالية بالتدريج موزعة على الحوادث الواقعة

TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r1.claim: Qur’an 17:106 says the Qur’an was divided so it could be recited to people over time; this is the pattern of gradual descent meant here.
TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r1.anchor: وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا

TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r2.claim: A possible objection is that slow, separated lessons let earlier material fade and weaken the learner’s resolve, while connected parts aid understanding and retention.
TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r2.anchor: يفسد غرض التعليم لانقطاع أثر السابق إلى أن يلحق به اللاحق وسقوط الهمة والعزيمة

TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r3.claim: Tartīl answers that concern: although revealed in portions, the lessons follow one another without severing their links or effects, preserving the purpose of instruction.
TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r3.anchor: عقبنا بعضها ببعض ونزلنا بعضها إثر بعض بحيث لا تبطل الروابط ولا نقطع آثار الأبعاض

TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r6.claim: The answer gives two reasons for gradual revelation: strengthening the Prophet’s heart and clarifying truth or correcting distorted interpretations for people.
TABATABAI:25:32-33#2/r6.anchor: جواب عن قولهم { لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة } بوجهين أحدهما بيان السبب الراجع إلى النبي

TABRISI:25:31-34/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:31-34/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:31-34/r4.claim: Tartīl is clear explanation delivered calmly and successively.

TABRISI:25:31-34/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:31-34/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:31-34/r5.claim: A tooth described as ratl or ratil is spaced and has no crowding or gaps.
TABRISI:25:31-34/r5.anchor: وثغر رتل ورتل بفتح التاء وسكونها إذا كان مفلجا لا لصص فيه

TABRISI:25:31-34/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:31-34/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:31-34/r10.claim: Jumlatan is accusative as a circumstantial expression meaning all together; aḥsana is genitive, coordinated with al-ḥaqq.
TABRISI:25:31-34/r10.anchor: جملة نصب على الحال معناه مجموعا وأحسن مجرور بالعطف على الحق

TABRISI:25:31-34/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:31-34/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:31-34/r21.claim: The disbelievers asked why the Quran was not delivered to Muhammad all at once, as they said the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms had been.
TABRISI:25:31-34/r21.anchor: هلا أتيتنا بالقرآن جملة واحدة كما أنزلت التوراة والإنجيل والزبور جملة واحدة

TABRISI:25:31-34/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:31-34/r22.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:31-34/r22.claim: God sent it gradually to strengthen the Prophet's heart: fresh revelation for each event increased his certainty and insight.
TABRISI:25:31-34/r22.anchor: أي لنقوي به قلبك فتزداد بصيرة

TABRISI:25:32/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:32/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:32/r1.claim: One explanation is that earlier books came down written because their prophets could read and write, whereas the unlettered Prophet received the Quran in installments.
TABRISI:25:32/r1.anchor: لأنها نزلت على الأنبياء يكتبون ويقرؤون فنزلت عليهم مكتوبة والقرآن إنما نزل على نبي أمي لا يكتب ولا يقرأ

TABRISI:25:32/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:32/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:32/r2.claim: Gradual revelation also fits the Quran's abrogating and abrogated rulings, answers to questions, corrections of events, and reports of happenings.
TABRISI:25:32/r2.anchor: وأيضا فإن في القرآن الناسخ والمنسوخ وفيه ما هو جواب لمن سأله عن أمور

TABRISI:25:32/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:32/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
TABRISI:25:32/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada explain tartīl as clear explanation and sending the revelation successively, one part after another.
TABRISI:25:32/r3.anchor: أي بيناه تبيينا وأرسلناه ترسيلا بعضه في أثر بعض عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:25:32/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:32/r4.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:25:32/r4.claim: Al-Suddī explains the phrase as setting the Quran out distinctly.

TABRISI:25:32/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:32/r5.speaker: النخعي
TABRISI:25:32/r5.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī explains it as dividing the Quran into parts.

TABRISI:25:32/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:32/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:25:32/r6.claim: The Prophet told Ibn Abbas to recite clearly, not scatter or rush the words like poetry, pause at its marvels, and move hearts rather than merely finish a sūra.
TABRISI:25:32/r6.anchor: وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

FARRA:v2p267/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p267/r4.speaker: الذين كفروا
FARRA:v2p267/r4.claim: The disbelievers ask why the Qur’an was not sent down all at once, as the Torah was sent to Moses.
FARRA:v2p267/r4.anchor: أي هلا أنزل عليه القرآن جملة، كما أنزلت التوراة على موسى.

FARRA:v2p267/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p267/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p267/r5.claim: One parse keeps كذلك within the disbelievers’ speech.

FARRA:v2p267/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p267/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p267/r6.claim: Alternatively, their speech ends at جملة واحدة and كذلك begins God’s response.
FARRA:v2p267/r6.anchor: ويقال: إن (كذلك) من قول الله، انقطع الكلام من قيلهم (جملة واحدة)

FARRA:v2p267/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p267/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p267/r7.claim: The Qur’an came piecemeal to steady the Prophet; one or two verses arrived at a time across twenty years.
FARRA:v2p267/r7.anchor: كان ينزل الآية والآيتين فمكان بين نزول أوله وآخره عشرون سنة

FARRA:v2p267/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p267/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p267/r8.claim: رتلناه means We sent it down successively.
FARRA:v2p267/r8.anchor: والآيتين فمكان بين نزول أوله وآخره عشرون سنة (ورتلناه ترتيلا) نزلناه تنزيلا.

THALABI:v7p132/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p132/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p132/r6.claim: The disbelievers ask why the Quran was not sent all at once, like the Torah, Psalms, and Gospel; God says gradual revelation strengthens Muhammad's heart so he can absorb and retain it.
THALABI:v7p132/r6.anchor: وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه على محمد القرآن جملة واحدة كما أنزلت التوراة على موسى

THALABI:v7p132/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p132/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p132/r7.claim: Earlier prophets could read and write, but Muhammad was unlettered; the Quran also contains abrogating and abrogated material and answers questions, so portions were separated to help him retain it and people receive it.
THALABI:v7p132/r7.anchor: فإن الكتب نزلت على أنبياء يكتبون ويقرءون، والقرآن أنزل على نبي أمي ولأن من القرآن الناسخ والمنسوخ

THALABI:v7p132/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p132/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p132/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses rattalnahu as sending it in successive portions.

THALABI:v7p132/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p132/r9.speaker: النخعي والحسن
THALABI:v7p132/r9.claim: Al-Nakha'i and al-Hasan say the Quran was divided verse by verse and thing by thing over about twenty-three years.
THALABI:v7p132/r9.anchor: وقال النخعي والحسن: فرقناه تفريقا آية بعد آية وشيئا بعد شيء، وكان بين أوله وآخره نحو ثلاث وعشرين سنة

THALABI:v7p132/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p132/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v7p132/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses tartil as making the Quran's meaning clear and explaining it.
THALABI:v7p132/r10.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: وفسرناه تفسيرا، والترتيل: التبيين في ترسل وتثبت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī reports that Quraysh challenged Muhammad to bring the Qur'an all at once like the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms; this verse was revealed in response.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: كانت كفار قريش يأتون رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- فيتعنتونه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r2.claim: Their request means that the Qur'an should have been sent at one time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r2.anchor: والمعنى: هلا نزل عليه القرآن في وقت واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj reads كذلك as God's answer for gradual revelation: their request asks why it came in installments, and the answer is to strengthen Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: أنزلناه كذلك متفرقا؛ لأن معنى قولهم: {لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة} يدل على معنى: لم نزل عليه القرآن متفرقا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r4.speaker: قوم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r4.claim: Some take كذلك as part of the disbelievers' statement, meaning like earlier scriptures; this reading requires omitted wording for the syntax.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r4.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن قوله: {كذلك} من كلام المشركين؛ فقالوا: إنهم قالوا: {لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة كذلك} أي: كالتوراة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r5.claim: Gradual revelation strengthened Muhammad's heart and insight; receiving it in response to events reinforced him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r5.anchor: ليصح النظم، وهو أن نقول: تقديره: أنزلناه متفرقا لنثبت به فؤادك (¬1). أى: ليقوى به قلبك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses strengthening the heart as comforting and encouraging Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p488/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: {لنثبت به فؤادك} أي: لنطيب به نفسك، ونشجعك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the wording as making the Qur'an clear.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r2.speaker: إبراهيم، الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r2.claim: Ibrāhīm and al-Ḥasan understand it as sending the Qur'an down in portions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r2.anchor: وقال إبراهيم: فرقناه في التنزيل (¬6). وهو معنى قول الحسن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r3.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r3.claim: Al-Suddī glosses it as explaining the Qur'an in detail.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says it was sent down with measured recitation, the opposite of haste.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: أنزلناه على الترتيل؛ وهو: ضد العجلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r5.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r5.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says tartīl is precise verification and clarification.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r5.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: ما أعلم الترتيل إلا التحقيق والتبيين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r6.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r6.claim: Al-Layth defines ratl as arrangement; speaking with tartīl is deliberate, well-composed, and paced so each part follows the last.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r6.anchor: قال الليث: الرتل، بفتح التاء: تنسيق الشيء. وثغر رتل، حسن المتنضد.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r7.claim: Mujāhid explains tartīl as sending the Qur'an down piece by piece, each portion following the preceding one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r7.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مجاهد، في تفسير الترتيل: بعضه على أثر بعض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r8.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r8.claim: The commentators say about twenty-three years separated the first revelation from the last.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r8.anchor: قال المفسرون: وكان بين أول نزول القرآن، وآخره، نحو من: ثلاث وعشرين سنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r9.claim: The Torah came all at once because it was written for a literate prophet; the Qur'an came gradually to an unlettered prophet and includes abrogation and answers to questions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p492/r9.anchor: وإنما أنزلت التوراة جملة؛ لأنها نزلت مكتوبة، على نبي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:27-32/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:27-32/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:27-32/r7.claim: Disbelievers objected that the Qur'an was revealed in portions instead of all at once, as they said the Torah and Gospel were.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:27-32/r7.anchor: أي: لم نزل عليه متفرقا؟ وهلا كان دفعة واحدة كالتوراة والإنجيل؟

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:27-32/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:27-32/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:27-32/r8.claim: Its gradual revelation strengthened the Prophet's heart as each new revelation came; God made its delivery clear, measured, and unhurried.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:27-32/r8.anchor: لنقوي به قلبك، وذلك أنه كلما نزل عليه وحي جديد ازداد هو قوة قلب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:27-32/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:27-32/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:27-32/r9.claim: The Qur'an was made clear through steady, measured delivery.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:27-32/r9.anchor: ورتلناه ترتيلا } بيناه تبيينا في تثبت ومهلة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r2.anchor: قوله: {وقال الذين كفروا لولا} [الفرقان: 32] يعني هلا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r3.claim: Qatadah says the unbelievers asked why the Qur'an was not sent down all at once as the Torah and Gospel were.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: أي كما أنزل على موسى وعلى عيسى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r4.claim: God explains that the staged revelation was to steady Muhammad's heart; the Qur'an was revealed over twenty-three years.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r4.anchor: قال الله: {كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك ورتلناه ترتيلا} [الفرقان: 32] قال قتادة: وبيناه تبيينا. نزل في ثلاث وعشرين سنة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p480/r5.claim: Qatadah glosses the measured recitation as making the Qur'an clear, clarification after clarification.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r1.claim: The Quran came down in stages across twenty-three years to ease people into duties, awaken them with recurring admonition, and test submission and discernment through abrogation.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r1.anchor: وأما تكرار الأنباء والقصص، فإن الله تبارك وتعالى أنزل القرآن نجوما

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r2.claim: Though تثبيت addresses the Prophet, it is intended for him and the believers; repeated revelation also prevents people tiring of one long admonition.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r2.anchor: الخطاب للنبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم، والمراد بالتثبيت هو والمؤمنون.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r3.claim: The Prophet attended to his companions with admonition at intervals so they would not weary, especially when heedlessness and hardened hearts set in.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r3.anchor: وكان رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، يتخول أصحابه بالموعظة مخافة السآمة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r4.claim: A single simultaneous revelation would precede its occasions, burden Muslims and converts with all duties at once, erase reminders, and make staged abrogation impossible.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r4.anchor: ولو أتاهم القرآن نجما واحدا لسبق حدوث الأسباب التي أنزله الله بها،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r5.claim: People need not memorize the whole Quran or complete a full reading; they should act on clear passages, believe ambiguous ones, obey commands, avoid prohibitions, and recite what they can in prayer.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r5.anchor: ولم يفرض الله على عباده أن يحفظوا القرآن كله، ولا أن يختموه في التعلم،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says the Quran was sent down to be acted upon, but people made reciting it their act.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r6.anchor: قال الحسن: نزل القرآن ليعمل به، فاتخذ الناس تلاوته عملا.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r7.claim: Most Companions learned portions rather than the whole Quran; only a few were enabled to collect and memorize it all.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r7.anchor: وكان أصحاب رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، ورضي عنهم- وهم مصابيح الأرض

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r8.claim: Anas reports that a man who had recited al-Baqara and Al Imran was held in great esteem by the Companions.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r8.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك: كان الرجل إذا قرأ البقرة وآل عمران جد فينا.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r9.speaker: الشعبي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r9.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali died without having collected the Quran.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p148/r9.anchor: قال الشعبي: توفى أبو بكر، وعمر، وعلي، رحمهم الله، ولم يجمعوا

MAJAZ:v2p74/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p74/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p74/r1.claim: The gradual sending is to comfort and encourage the Prophet’s heart.
MAJAZ:v2p74/r1.anchor: لنثبت به فؤادك» (32) مجازه لنطيب به نفسك ونشجعك.

ELMALILI:25:31-33/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r2.claim: The demand for one-time revelation is a meaningless objection, as though the Torah had been revealed all at once; the Quran's inimitability is unaffected by gradual delivery.
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r2.anchor: güya Tevrat birden indirilmiş de Kur’an da öyle olsa imiş. Hâlbuki rûh-ı mesele olan i‘câz

ELMALILI:25:31-33/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r3.claim: Gradual revelation first strengthens the Prophet's heart by making the Quran easier to retain and memorize.
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r3.anchor: evvelâ zabt u hıfzı sağlam olacak, sâniyen peyderpey vekāyi‘e göre inişinde mâna itibariyle daha ziyade bir basiret

ELMALILI:25:31-33/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r4.claim: Revelation in response to events gives its meanings greater insight and depth, with theoretical and practical value and strength.
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r4.anchor: sâniyen peyderpey vekāyi‘e göre inişinde mâna itibariyle daha ziyade bir basiret ve derinlik, hem nazarî ve hem amelî

ELMALILI:25:31-33/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r5.claim: Each new portion poses another challenge that leaves opponents unable to match it and renews the Prophet's strength of heart.
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r5.anchor: her yeni inen necm ile ayrıca bir tehaddî yapılıp mu‘ârazasından âciz bırakılmakla her birinde yeni bir kuvvet-i kalb verilecek

ELMALILI:25:31-33/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r6.claim: Gradual revelation teaches legislation suited to its time through abrogating and abrogated rulings, along with varied methods and principles of explanation and commentary.
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r6.anchor: nâsih ve mensuh ile zamânına göre ahkâm teşrî‘i, beyan ve tefsîrin usûl ve kavâ‘id-i mütenevvi‘ası öğretilecek

ELMALILI:25:31-33/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r7.claim: Tartil is an unmatched, measured, beautiful recitation, delivered slowly and well.
ELMALILI:25:31-33/r7.anchor: ve emsâlsiz bir tertil ile tertil eyledik ağır ağır, güzel bir okuyuş okuduk

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r1.claim: The polytheists’ demand that the Qur’an be revealed all at once is another excuse for disbelief; even that would not make them believe, since they sought to protect false beliefs and material and social interests.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r1.anchor: Aslında Kur’an’ın hepsi birden indirilseydi onlar yine inanmayacaklardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r2.claim: This tactic is not unique to pre-Islamic idolaters: some people today conceal their aims behind seemingly innocent demands, as if granting them would make them devout.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r2.anchor: bu tutum sadece Câhiliye müşriklerine özgü bir hal de değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r3.claim: Although God knows their true intent, the verse briefly answers because the demand might confuse sincere people; gradual revelation over about twenty-three years let each passage settle in the Prophet’s mind and soul.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r3.anchor: Kur’an’ın tamamını bir defada değil de yaklaşık yirmi üç sene zarfında, âyet âyet, bölüm bölüm indirmekle Resûlullah’ın her gelen âyeti gerek metni gerekse anlamıyla zihnine iyice yerleştirmesini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r4.claim: The Prophet fully memorized the Qur’an accurately and made its principles, beginning with faith, part of his character before conveying them to others.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r4.anchor: Kur’an’ın bütününü eksiksiz ve yanlışsız olarak hâfızasına yerleştirdiği gibi, diğer insanlara tebliğ etmeden önce bizzat kendisi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r5.speaker: Hz. Âişe
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r5.claim: Aisha described the Prophet’s character as the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:32/r5.anchor: Hz. Âişe’nin ifadesiyle Kur’an onun ahlâkı haline gelmiştir (Müslim, “Müsâfirîn”, 139)

ITQAN:v4p417/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p417/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري والقاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
ITQAN:v4p417/r1.claim: Al-Ashʿari and al-Baqillani prohibit ranking Quran passages, since all are God’s speech and ranking could imply deficiency in the less-favored passage.
ITQAN:v4p417/r1.anchor: فذهب الإمام أبو الحسن الأشعري والقاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني وابن حبان إلى المنع لأن الجميع كلام الله

ITQAN:v4p417/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p417/r2.speaker: مالك ويحيى بن يحيى
ITQAN:v4p417/r2.claim: Yahya b. Yahya calls preferring some Quran passages over others an error; Malik disliked repeatedly reciting one sura to the exclusion of others.
ITQAN:v4p417/r2.anchor: وروي هذا القول عن مالك قال يحيى بن يحيى تفضيل بعض القرآن على بعض خطأ ولذلك كره مالك

ITQAN:v4p417/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p417/r3.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v4p417/r3.claim: Ibn Hibban reads the report that al-Fatiha is the greatest sura as referring to its reward, not to intrinsic superiority among Quran passages.
ITQAN:v4p417/r3.anchor: وقال ابن حبان في حديث أبي بن كعب ما أنزل الله في التوراة ولا في الإنجيل مثل أم القرآن

ITQAN:v4p417/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p417/r4.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v4p417/r4.claim: Ibn Hibban explains the greater reward for al-Fatiha by God’s special favor to this community in the reward for reciting revelation.
ITQAN:v4p417/r4.anchor: إن الله لا يعطي لقارئ التوراة والإنجيل من الثواب مثل ما يعطي القارئ أم القرآن إذ الله سبحانه وتعالى بفضله فضل هذه الأمة

ITQAN:v4p417/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p417/r5.speaker: إسحاق بن راهويه وأبو بكر بن العربي والغزالي
ITQAN:v4p417/r5.claim: Ishaq b. Rahawayh, Ibn al-Arabi, and al-Ghazali permit ranking Quran passages, relying on the apparent meaning of the hadiths.
ITQAN:v4p417/r5.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى التفضيل لظواهر الأحاديث منهم إسحاق بن راهوية وأبو بكر بن العربي والغزالي

ITQAN:v4p417/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p417/r6.speaker: القرطبي
ITQAN:v4p417/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi says that ranking passages is the correct position and attributes it to a group of scholars and theologians.
ITQAN:v4p417/r6.anchor: وقال القرطبي إنه الحق ونقله عن جماعة من العلماء والمتكلمين

ITQAN:v4p417/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p417/r7.speaker: الغزالي
ITQAN:v4p417/r7.claim: Al-Ghazali argues that the Prophet’s reports establish differences in merit, citing Yasin, al-Fatiha, Ayat al-Kursi, and al-Ikhlas as specially meritorious.
ITQAN:v4p417/r7.anchor: وقال الغزالي في جواهر القرآن لعلك أن تقول قد أشرت إلى تفضيل بعض آيات القرآن على بعض

ITQAN:v4p417/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p417/r8.speaker: ابن الحصار
ITQAN:v4p417/r8.claim: Ibn al-Hassar wonders why scholars report disagreement despite explicit texts that rank some Quran passages above others.
ITQAN:v4p417/r8.anchor: وقال ابن الحصار العجب ممن يذكر الاختلاف في ذلك مع النصوص الواردة بالتفضيل

ITQAN:v1p119/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p119/r1.speaker: أبو شامة
ITQAN:v1p119/r1.claim: Abu Shama suggests that the position under discussion was meant to reconcile the first two positions on how the Quran was sent down.
ITQAN:v1p119/r1.anchor: وقال أبو شامة كأن صاحب هذا القول أراد الجمع بين القولين الأول والثاني

ITQAN:v1p119/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p119/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p119/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Quran descended all at once from the Preserved Tablet to the scribes in the lowest heaven; they sent it in installments to Gabriel over twenty nights, and Gabriel delivered it to the Prophet over twenty years.
ITQAN:v1p119/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال نزل القرآن جملة واحدة من عند الله من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السفرة الكرام الكاتبين في السماء الدنيا

NAHHAS:v3p159/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p159/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p159/r3.claim: If the pause is at جملة واحدة, لِنثبت is understood as “for strengthening”; if at كذلك, ورتلناه ترتيلا كذلك means “We arranged it in that manner.”
NAHHAS:v3p159/r3.anchor: هذا على أن يكون التمام عند قوله جل وعز ( جملة واحدة ) وإن كان التمام عند كذلك كان التقدير ترتيلا كذلك

NAHHAS:v3p159/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p159/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p159/r4.claim: Unable to disprove the Prophet with proof, the disbelievers demanded one complete revelation; gradual answers to their questions were a prophetic sign and strengthened his heart and theirs.
NAHHAS:v3p159/r4.anchor: لما لم يجد المشركون سبيلا إلى تكذيب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ببرهان ولا حجة

NAHHAS:v3p159/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p159/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p159/r7.claim: Al-Naḥḥās prefers pausing at جملة واحدة; pausing at كذلك makes “likewise” point to the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms without prior mention.
NAHHAS:v3p159/r7.anchor: والأولى أن يكون التمام جملة واحدة لأنه إذا وقف على كذلك صار المعنى كالتوراة والإنجيل والزبور ولم يتقدم لهما ذكر

NAHHAS:v3p159/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p159/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p159/r8.claim: Abū Isḥāq says tartīl means slow, measured delivery, the opposite of haste.
NAHHAS:v3p159/r8.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق ورتلناه ترتيلا أي أنزلناه قيل الترتيل وهو التمكث وهو ضد العجلة

BURHAN:v2p193/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p193/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p193/r5.claim: The objection to gradual revelation is answered by explaining that the Qur'an was divided so it could be recited to people at a measured pace.
BURHAN:v2p193/r5.anchor: ﴿ وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة ﴾ فقيل فى سورة أخرى

ITQAN:v1p121/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p121/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p121/r1.claim: One explanation says the Qurʾan came in portions to preserve it in the heart of the unlettered Prophet, who could not read or write, unlike literate earlier prophets.
ITQAN:v1p121/r1.anchor: وقيل معنى ﴿ لنثبت به فؤادك ﴾ أي لنحفظه فإنه عليه السلام كان أميا لا يقرأ ولا يكتب

ITQAN:v1p121/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p121/r2.speaker: ابن فورك
ITQAN:v1p121/r2.claim: Ibn Furak explains that the Torah descended as a whole to the literate Moses, while the Qurʾan descended piecemeal because it was sent unwritten to an unlettered Prophet.
ITQAN:v1p121/r2.anchor: وقال ابن فورك قيل أنزلت التوراة جملة لأنها نزلت على نبي يكتب ويقرأ

ITQAN:v1p121/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p121/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p121/r3.claim: Another explanation is that gradual revelation permits abrogation and responds to questions and objections as they arise; Ibn Abbas says Gabriel brought answers to people’s words and deeds, explaining the verse about answering their examples with truth.
ITQAN:v1p121/r3.anchor: إنما لم ينزل جملة واحدة لأن منه الناسخ والمنسوخ ولا يتأتى ذلك إلا فيما أنزل مفرقا

ITQAN:v1p121#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p121#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p121#2/r1.claim: The common scholarly view is that earlier scriptures were revealed all at once; an unnamed contemporary objected that there is no proof and argued that they descended gradually like the Qur'an.
ITQAN:v1p121#2/r1.anchor: ما تقدم في كلام هؤلاء من أن سائر الكتب أنزلت جملة هو مشهور في كلام العلماء

ITQAN:v1p121#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p121#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p121#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Jews asked Muḥammad why the Qur'an was not sent all at once as the Torah was to Moses; another version attributes the question to polytheists, with similar reports from Qatāda and al-Suddī.
ITQAN:v1p121#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قالت اليهود يا أبا القاسم لولا أنزل هذا القرآن جملة واحدة

ITQAN:v1p121#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p121#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p121#2/r3.claim: Al-Suyūṭī prefers the view that previous scriptures came all at once, arguing that God's silence on the premise and turn to explain the Qur'an's wisdom support it.
ITQAN:v1p121#2/r3.anchor: وأقول الصواب الأول ومن الأدلة على ذلك آية الفرقان السابقة

ITQAN:v1p121#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p121#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p121#2/r4.claim: He argues that if earlier books had descended gradually, God could have answered by citing that precedent, as He answers other objections by noting earlier messengers ate, were human men, and had wives and children.
ITQAN:v1p121#2/r4.anchor: ولو كانت الكتب كلها نزلت مفرقة لكان يكفي في الرد عليهم أن يقول إن ذلك سنة الله في الكتب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1067/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1067/r3.speaker: قسم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1067/r3.claim: Some distinguish anzala as a one-time descent and nazzala as gradual revelation; grammarians object that the Quran itself uses nazzala for a single, complete descent.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1067/r3.anchor: قسم يقولون أنزل أي كله جملة واحدة ونزّل منجماً لكن قسم من النحاة ردوا على هذا القول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r8.speaker: ساداتنا الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r8.claim: They take “the wise Quran” as divine realities that the servant realizes and ascends through step by step; the ascent continues as God’s self-disclosure continues.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r8.anchor: وأما القرآن الحكيم فهوية الحقائق الإلهية يعرج العبد بالتحقيق بها في الذات شيئا فشيئا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r7.speaker: عمر وهشام بن حكيم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r7.claim: On the condition that the report reliably conveys Umar's purpose rather than paraphrasing away its point, the hadith of Umar and Hisham may support a different explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r7.anchor: وعندي أنه إن كان حديث عمر وهشام بن حكيم قد حسن إفصاح راويه عن مقصد عمر فيما حدث به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r8.claim: Ibn Ashur hypothesizes that the concession concerned the order of verses within surahs: Hisham recited al-Furqan in a different order from Umar, allowing memorization without fixed verse order.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r8.anchor: أنه يحتمل أن يرجع إلى ترتيب آي السور بأن يكون هشام قرأ سورة الفرقان على غير الترتيب الذي قرأ به عمر

BURHAN:v1p231/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p231/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p231/r1.claim: God answers the demand for a single revelation by explaining that gradual revelation strengthens the Prophet's heart; new revelation at each event renews care, reassurance, and his connection with the angel and message.
BURHAN:v1p231/r1.anchor: أى لنقوى به قلبك فإن الوحى إذا كان يتجدد فى كل حادثة كان أقوى للقلب

BURHAN:v1p231/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p231/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p231/r2.claim: The repeated arrival of Gabriel brought the Prophet joy, and the text connects this to his exceptional generosity in Ramadan, when Gabriel came more often.
BURHAN:v1p231/r2.anchor: وتجديد العهد به وبما معه من الرسالة الواردة من ذلك الجانب العزيز فحدث له من السرور ما تقصر عنه العبارة

BURHAN:v1p231/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p231/r3.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v1p231/r3.claim: Another explanation is that gradual revelation helped the unlettered Prophet memorize the Qur'an, unlike literate prophets who could retain a complete revelation at once.
BURHAN:v1p231/r3.anchor: لنحفظه فإنه عليه السلام كان اميا لا يقرأ ولا يكتب ففرق عليه

BURHAN:v1p231/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p231/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p231/r4.claim: Although God could have enabled the Prophet to memorize the whole Qur'an at once, not every possible event has to occur; questions and the need for abrogation also account for piecemeal revelation.
BURHAN:v1p231/r4.anchor: قلت ليس كل ممكن لازم الوقوع وأيضا فى القرآن أجوبة عن أسئلة فهو سبب من أسباب تفرق النزول ولأن بعضه منسوخ وبعضه ناسخ

BURHAN:v1p231/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p231/r5.speaker: ابن فورك
BURHAN:v1p231/r5.claim: Ibn Furak reports that the Torah came down at once to literate Moses, whereas the unwritten Qur'an came gradually to an unlettered Prophet; he also cites abrogation, answers to questions, and timely denials.
BURHAN:v1p231/r5.anchor: وقال ابن فورك قيل أنزلت التوراة جملة لأنها نزلت على نبى يقرأ ويكتب وهو موسى وأنزل القرآن مفرقا

BURHAN:v1p231/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p231/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p231/r6.claim: The interval from the first to last revelation is given as twenty, twenty-three, or twenty-five years, depending on whether the Prophet lived in Mecca after the call for ten, thirteen, or fifteen years; his Medina period was ten years.
BURHAN:v1p231/r6.anchor: وكان بين أول نزول القرآن آخره عشرون أو ثلاث وعشرون أو خمس وعشرون سنة وهو مبنى على الخلاف فى مدة إقامته صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة

BURHAN:v1p231/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p231/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p231/r7.claim: Whenever revelation came, the Prophet ordered it written and specified the surah where separate verses belonged.
BURHAN:v1p231/r7.anchor: وكان كلما أنزل عليه شىء من القرآن أمر بكتابته ويقول فى مفترقات الآيات ضعوا هذه فى سورة كذا

BURHAN:v1p231/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p231/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p231/r8.claim: Gabriel reviewed the Qur'an with the Prophet once each Ramadan and twice in the year he died.
BURHAN:v1p231/r8.anchor: وكان يعرضه جبريل فى شهر رمضان كل عام مرة وعام مات مرتين
